# 1. What's Moving and What Triggered It

MONITORING

The Gallery Climate Coalition (GCC) has moved from a single-market charity into standard-setting and, now, paid-consultancy infrastructure for the global visual arts sector. Three developments define the current signal.

**GCC's first Stocktake Report (14 November 2025).** The captured source states, verbatim: "four fifths of its members that began tracking their carbon output in 2019 have reduced it by more than 25%" This puts them on course to halve their emissions by 2030. *Source: The Art Newspaper, 14 November 2025. https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2025/11/14/most-gallery-climate-coalition-members-on-track-halve-carbon-emissions-2030-report* The report projects a sector-wide reduction potential: the captured source states, verbatim: "the global art sector could collectively cut more than five million tonnes of CO₂ a year" *Source: The Art Newspaper, 14 November 2025. https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2025/11/14/most-gallery-climate-coalition-members-on-track-halve-carbon-emissions-2030-report* The report was released to coincide with a new event: the captured source states, verbatim: "was launched to coincide with London Art+Climate Week —a new five-day event running parallel to the United Nations climate summit Cop30 in Brazil." *Source: The Art Newspaper, 14 November 2025. https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2025/11/14/most-gallery-climate-coalition-members-on-track-halve-carbon-emissions-2030-report*

**Launch of Climate Action Services International (Casi), 22 April 2026.** The captured source states, verbatim: "GCC revealed the next step in its growth with the launch of a new consultancy called Climate Action Services International (Casi)." *Source: The Art Newspaper, 22 April 2026. https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2026/04/22/gallery-climate-coalition-launching-consultancy-casi* The article's own byline dates this, verbatim: "Annabel Keenan 22 April 2026" *Source: The Art Newspaper, 22 April 2026. https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2026/04/22/gallery-climate-coalition-launching-consultancy-casi* The captured source states, verbatim: "With a remit of helping galleries, museums and cultural organisations translate climate commitments into measurable action, the launch of Casi reflects a growing recognition that ambition alone is no longer sufficient to decarbonise complex, globally dispersed operations." *Source: The Art Newspaper, 22 April 2026. https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2026/04/22/gallery-climate-coalition-launching-consultancy-casi*

**Art Fair Co-Commitment Statement (2 October 2024).** The captured source states, verbatim: "13 organisations representing more than 40 art fairs have committed to a consensus on new standards of operating." *Source: FAD Magazine, 2 October 2024. https://fadmagazine.com/2024/10/02/gallery-climate-coalition-announces-art-fair-co-commitment-statement/* (byline: "By Mark Westall • 2 October 2024" *Source: FAD Magazine, 2 October 2024. https://fadmagazine.com/2024/10/02/gallery-climate-coalition-announces-art-fair-co-commitment-statement/*)

**What triggered it.** The captured source states, verbatim: "GCC was founded in London in February 2020." *Source: UNFCCC, "Art Charter for Climate Action." https://unfccc.int/climate-action/sectoral-engagement/entertainment-and-culture-for-climate-action/art-charter-for-climate-action* *Analytical inference:* GCC's own membership organisation, launched in 2020 with a five-year target horizon to 2030, is now producing three converging artifacts within roughly eighteen months of each other (the Stocktake Report, the Casi consultancy, and the Art Fair Co-Commitment Statement) rather than one at a time -- a sign the sector is moving from voluntary self-reporting toward measured, funded implementation.

*Operational implication:* for workspaces whose clients are commercial galleries, museums, or art fairs -- fine art logistics is the primary vertical here -- these three developments together signal that freight partners will increasingly be asked for the same measured, reportable emissions data GCC members are now producing internally.

# 2. Who's Driving It and What They Want

The captured source states, verbatim: "The Gallery Climate Coalition (GCC) is an international charity and membership organisation providing environmental sustainability guidelines for the global visual art sector." *Source: UNFCCC, "Art Charter for Climate Action." https://unfccc.int/climate-action/sectoral-engagement/entertainment-and-culture-for-climate-action/art-charter-for-climate-action*

**GCC's steering position.** The captured source states, verbatim: "The current steering committee is comprised of ART 2030, the Gallery Climate Coalition, and Julie’s Bicycle, who have a combined representation of over 1000 members in over 70 countries." *Source: UNFCCC, "Art Charter for Climate Action." https://unfccc.int/climate-action/sectoral-engagement/entertainment-and-culture-for-climate-action/art-charter-for-climate-action* *Analytical inference:* GCC is one of three co-equal bodies steering the UNFCCC-hosted charter, not a standalone actor -- ART 2030 and Julie's Bicycle share governance and, through Julie's Bicycle, the measurement tooling.

**Julie's Bicycle (parallel measurement infrastructure).** The captured source states, verbatim: "Launched in 2009, the Creative Climate Tools (formerly known as Creative Green Tools) are free and open to anyone in the arts and culture sector worldwide" *Source: Julie's Bicycle, "Creative Climate Tools." https://juliesbicycle.com/our-work/creative-green/creative-climate-tools/* The captured source further states, verbatim: "Over 2,000 organisations across more than 20 countries are already using the Creative Climate Tools" *Source: Julie's Bicycle, "Creative Climate Tools." https://juliesbicycle.com/our-work/creative-green/creative-climate-tools/* Julie's Bicycle's own homepage states, verbatim: "Julie’s Bicycle is an international non-profit uniting culture, creativity and climate action to drive change." *Source: Julie's Bicycle. https://juliesbicycle.com/*

**Major art fairs (demand-side pressure on the supply chain).** The captured source names every signatory, verbatim: "The art fair signatories of the Art Fair Co-Commitment Statement are: ARCO, Art Basel, CHART, Easyfairs, ESTE ARTE, Frieze, Liste Art Fair Basel, Market Art Fair, Ramsay Fairs, STAGE Bregenz, TEFAF, The Art Show & Untitled Art." *Source: FAD Magazine, 2 October 2024. https://fadmagazine.com/2024/10/02/gallery-climate-coalition-announces-art-fair-co-commitment-statement/* *Analytical inference:* this is not a symbolic list -- Art Basel, Frieze, and TEFAF are named alongside ten other fairs, meaning the co-commitment reaches the largest transaction volumes in the international art-fair calendar, and freight partners serving any of those twelve named fairs are serving a signatory's own stated 2030 commitment whether or not the workspace itself has been told so directly.

**Casi (the implementation delivery vehicle).** Two captured sources name the same individual differently. The captured source identifies him as, verbatim: "Heath Lowndes, Director, Gallery Climate Coalition" *Source: FAD Magazine, 2 October 2024. https://fadmagazine.com/2024/10/02/gallery-climate-coalition-announces-art-fair-co-commitment-statement/* A later captured source identifies the same named individual differently, verbatim: "Heath Lowndes, the founder of Casi" *Source: The Art Newspaper, 22 April 2026. https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2026/04/22/gallery-climate-coalition-launching-consultancy-casi* *Analytical inference:* read together, this is one person's own role moving from directing GCC itself to founding GCC's new consultancy arm -- consistent with, not contradictory to, the captured source's own account of Casi's origin. Named party Heath Lowndes is quoted verbatim in the captured source: "Right from the beginning, it was clear that while shared standards, tools and advocacy are essential, many organisations would require hands-on, tailored support to implement meaningful change. Over the past five years, that demand has grown significantly." *Source: The Art Newspaper, 22 April 2026. https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2026/04/22/gallery-climate-coalition-launching-consultancy-casi*

The captured source states, verbatim: "Casi bills itself as a “mission-driven social enterprise”, and has pledged to reinvest 51% of its profits into GCC." *Source: The Art Newspaper, 22 April 2026. https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2026/04/22/gallery-climate-coalition-launching-consultancy-casi* The captured source states, verbatim: "Casi joins a small group of climate consultants who have been supporting the art industry, including Ki Culture, Laura Lupton and Rute Collaborative." *Source: The Art Newspaper, 22 April 2026. https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2026/04/22/gallery-climate-coalition-launching-consultancy-casi* The captured source states, verbatim: "Casi will provide organisation-specific services including carbon auditing, decarbonisation strategies, governance advice and staff training." *Source: The Art Newspaper, 22 April 2026. https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2026/04/22/gallery-climate-coalition-launching-consultancy-casi*

# 3. Expected Trajectory and Conversion Triggers

WINDOW CLOSING

**Trajectory timeline.**
- 2 October 2024: GCC and a new alliance of art fairs announced the Art Fair Co-Commitment Statement.
- 27 September 2025: The Art Newspaper reported Frieze's own climate-fundraising initiative for its London fairs.
- 22 April 2026: GCC launched Climate Action Services International (Casi).

**Baseline target (already set, not speculative).** The captured source states, verbatim: "The coalition’s primary target is to facilitate a reduction of the visual art sector’s greenhouse gas emissions by a minimum of 50% by 2030 (in line with the Paris Agreement’s goal of keeping global warming to below 1.5°C) as well as promoting zero-waste practices." *Source: UNFCCC, "Art Charter for Climate Action." https://unfccc.int/climate-action/sectoral-engagement/entertainment-and-culture-for-climate-action/art-charter-for-climate-action* *Analytical inference:* every conversion trigger below operates inside this single already-adopted 2030 target -- none of them is a new obligation, each is a mechanism the sector is building to reach a target it committed to years ago.

**Conversion trigger 1 -- Frieze's own gallery fundraising pledge.** The captured source's own related-content item states, verbatim: "Frieze to launch climate change fundraising initiative at its London fairs" (dated: "Art fairs news 27 September 2025") *Source: The Art Newspaper, 14 November 2025. https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2025/11/14/most-gallery-climate-coalition-members-on-track-halve-carbon-emissions-2030-report* The captured source states, verbatim: "Participating galleries have signed up to pledge 10% of the sale price of selected works to fund the Gallery Climate Coalition" *Source: The Art Newspaper, 14 November 2025. https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2025/11/14/most-gallery-climate-coalition-members-on-track-halve-carbon-emissions-2030-report* *Operational implication:* a gallery client that has signed this pledge has already put a portion of its own sale proceeds behind GCC -- a workspace serving that gallery at a London fair season is serving a client with a live, named financial commitment to the same coalition driving this whole signal.

**Conversion trigger 2 -- the ACCA Signatory tier opening.** The captured source states, verbatim: "ACCA will be opened to interested Signatories in the near future." *Source: UNFCCC, "Art Charter for Climate Action." https://unfccc.int/climate-action/sectoral-engagement/entertainment-and-culture-for-climate-action/art-charter-for-climate-action* The captured source states, verbatim: "Signatories gain the opportunity to join the ACCA steering committee" *Source: UNFCCC, "Art Charter for Climate Action." https://unfccc.int/climate-action/sectoral-engagement/entertainment-and-culture-for-climate-action/art-charter-for-climate-action* *Legal Confirmation Required:* this brief does not resolve what commitments a Signatory takes on, or whether a freight-sector participant is eligible to sign -- that determination sits with the ACCA Community itself, not with this brief.

**Conversion trigger 3 -- the Art Fair Co-Commitment Statement's own decade-end target.** The captured source states, verbatim: "The Art Fair Co-Commitment Statement contains a commitment to at least a 50% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions by the end of the decade." *Source: FAD Magazine, 2 October 2024. https://fadmagazine.com/2024/10/02/gallery-climate-coalition-announces-art-fair-co-commitment-statement/* *Analytical inference:* twelve named art fairs (Section 2) now carry this same commitment independently of GCC's own 2030 target -- two overlapping deadlines converging on the same calendar year, which compounds rather than staggers the procurement pressure on freight partners serving both galleries and art fairs.

**Re-check window:** revisit when GCC opens the ACCA Signatory tier (no date given in the captured source) and after the next full art-fair season, when the Art Fair Co-Commitment Statement's own reporting cycle should first surface supplier-level data requests.

# 4. Operational and Cost Implications If It Materializes

MONITORING

This section filters through the workspace's operational profile: fine art and high-value cargo as a primary vertical, air freight as primary mode, road secondary, ocean tertiary.

**Air freight is the highest-exposure category.** The captured source states, verbatim: "a typical commercial gallery might expect one-third of its annual carbon emissions to be associated with art fair activities and air freight, specifically making up an estimated 70% of that figure" *Source: FAD Magazine, 2 October 2024. https://fadmagazine.com/2024/10/02/gallery-climate-coalition-announces-art-fair-co-commitment-statement/* *Operational implication:* air freight is described as the majority component of a meaningful share of a typical commercial gallery's total annual footprint. The captured source does not itself state a single combined percentage for air freight's own share of TOTAL gallery emissions; this brief accordingly states only the two figures the source itself gives (roughly one-third of annual emissions tied to art fair activity and air freight together, with air freight specifically making up an estimated 70% of that one-third) rather than compute and assert a derived total the source does not itself state.

**International shipping complexity.** The captured source states, verbatim: "where things like international shipping, temporary exhibitions and energy-intensive installations complicate emissions reduction efforts" *Source: The Art Newspaper, 22 April 2026. https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2026/04/22/gallery-climate-coalition-launching-consultancy-casi* *Operational implication:* workspaces moving art between major fair hubs handle exactly the transport leg GCC member institutions are trying to reduce and account for; the ability to hand a client standardised, per-shipment emissions data is the operational gap between where most freight partners are today and what Casi's own carbon-auditing work (Section 2) will surface as a client requirement.

**The GCC Carbon Calculator as the reporting chokepoint.** The captured source states, verbatim: "the Carbon Calculator is a crucial part of GCC’s provision of resources to galleries, garnering more than 18,000 users and becoming the foundation of arts organisations’ environmental impact monitoring and decarbonisation strategy." *Source: FAD Magazine, 2 October 2024. https://fadmagazine.com/2024/10/02/gallery-climate-coalition-announces-art-fair-co-commitment-statement/* *Operational implication:* a tool already used by more than 18,000 people is the de facto reporting format GCC-aligned galleries expect their own data, including freight data, to feed into.

**Carbon accounting methodology gap.** Academic research published in the captured source states, verbatim: "Defining the balance limits implies first determining which organisational units, e.g., an exhibition space or the lifecycle of a production, are included in the report and second identifying the direct and indirect emissions associated with this unit." *Source: European Journal of Cultural Management and Policy, 8 October 2025. https://www.frontierspartnerships.org/journals/european-journal-of-cultural-management-and-policy/articles/10.3389/ejcmp.2025.14629/full* The same captured source states, verbatim: "direct emission reductions are often constrained by the systemic limitations of arts organisations, with critical leverage points located at national and international levels" *Source: European Journal of Cultural Management and Policy, 8 October 2025. https://www.frontierspartnerships.org/journals/european-journal-of-cultural-management-and-policy/articles/10.3389/ejcmp.2025.14629/full* *Analytical inference:* if an art institution's own reporting boundary decision determines whether a given shipment's emissions count inside or outside its report, a freight partner that cannot say clearly which "organisational unit" (per-exhibition, per-loan, per-fair) its own shipment data maps to creates exactly the boundary-definition problem this peer-reviewed research identifies as a systemic constraint on the sector's own reductions.

**Cost of GCC-aligned emissions data provision.** *Specific cost figures for freight-specific emissions reporting tooling are not stated in this item's captured source pool.*

# 5. Competitive Implications

MONITORING

**Who is positioned to act as implementation partner.** The captured source states, verbatim: "Casi will provide organisation-specific services including carbon auditing, decarbonisation strategies, governance advice and staff training." *Source: The Art Newspaper, 22 April 2026. https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2026/04/22/gallery-climate-coalition-launching-consultancy-casi* These are institution-facing services, not freight-facing ones. *Analytical inference:* Casi, Ki Culture, Laura Lupton, and Rute Collaborative (Section 2) all sit on the institution side of the relationship, helping a gallery or museum understand and cut its own emissions -- none of the four is described in the captured source as a freight-side data provider, which leaves the shipment-level Scope 3 data question open for whichever freight partner answers it first.

**Named competitor activity.** No source in this item's captured pool names a specific competing freight forwarder's sustainability or Scope 3 data-provision positioning; the pool names only institution-facing climate consultancies (Casi, Ki Culture, Laura Lupton, Rute Collaborative), never a freight-facing competitor. This brief states that absence rather than inventing a competitor's position to appear complete.

**Who is at risk.** *Analytical inference:* workspaces serving GCC-aligned galleries or any of the twelve named Art Fair Co-Commitment signatories (Section 2), without a standardised way to hand over per-shipment emissions data, face rising pressure as the Art Fair Co-Commitment Statement's own decade-end target (Section 3) and GCC's own 2030 target (Section 3) converge on the same window.

# 6. Client Conversation Talking Points

**What the workspace can credibly say:**

- GCC's own Stocktake Report found that four-fifths of tracked members cut emissions by more than 25% since 2019, putting them on course to halve emissions by 2030, and that the sector overall could cut more than five million tonnes of CO2 a year (Section 1).
- Twelve named art fairs -- including Art Basel, Frieze, and TEFAF -- have committed to at least a 50% emissions reduction by the end of the decade under the Art Fair Co-Commitment Statement (Section 2, Section 3).
- GCC's own emissions data attributes roughly one-third of a typical commercial gallery's annual footprint to art fair activity and air freight together, with air freight making up an estimated 70% of that share (Section 4).
- GCC's own Carbon Calculator has more than 18,000 users and functions as the sector's default emissions-reporting tool (Section 4).

**Questions to pose to art-sector clients:**

- Is your organisation a GCC member, or a signatory to the Art Fair Co-Commitment Statement -- and if so, does your own reporting boundary include your freight partners' emissions?
- Has Casi, or another named consultant, asked your organisation for shipment-level data from your logistics partners as part of a carbon audit?
- Do you currently feed any data into the GCC Carbon Calculator, and if so, in what format?

**Pitfalls to avoid:**

- Do not claim GCC certification or endorsement for freight services -- the captured source describes no GCC freight-partner accreditation scheme.
- Do not cite the five-million-tonne figure as applying to freight specifically -- the captured source states it as the art sector's aggregate potential reduction across all emission sources.
- Do not assert a combined "air freight = X% of total gallery emissions" figure -- the captured source states only the two component figures (one-third of annual emissions tied to art fair activity and air freight together, air freight an estimated 70% of that share), and this brief does not multiply them into a number the source itself does not state.

# 7. What the Workspace Should Do Now

ACTION REQUIRED

**1. Treat the Casi launch as a near-term outreach window. (Immediate -- Casi launched 22 April 2026 and is, per its own remit, actively building institutional relationships.)** [action_now] The captured source states, verbatim: "With a remit of helping galleries, museums and cultural organisations translate climate commitments into measurable action, the launch of Casi reflects a growing recognition that ambition alone is no longer sufficient to decarbonise complex, globally dispersed operations." *Source: The Art Newspaper, 22 April 2026. https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2026/04/22/gallery-climate-coalition-launching-consultancy-casi* *Operational implication:* Casi's own carbon-auditing work (Section 2) will surface exactly the shipment-level data gap described in Section 4; a workspace that can hand Casi's client institutions standardised per-shipment emissions data ahead of that need is positioned as the answer to a problem Casi itself is about to identify for its clients.

**2. Map current shipment data output against the GCC Carbon Calculator's own input needs. (Strategic -- no regulatory deadline applies; the commercial window is open now, per Section 4.)** *Operational implication:* determine whether the workspace's existing shipment-level emissions data (fuel burn, tonne-km, emission factors) can be exported in a format that feeds a GCC-member client's own Carbon Calculator entry, given more than 18,000 people already use that tool.

**3. Identify the twelve named Art Fair Co-Commitment signatories the workspace already serves. (Immediate -- the signatory list is named in Section 2.)** *Operational implication:* a workspace already moving artwork for Art Basel, Frieze, TEFAF, or any of the other nine named fairs (Section 2) is already serving a client with a live, named 2030 commitment; confirm which of those relationships exist today.

**4. Monitor the ACCA Signatory tier opening. (Monitoring -- no date is given in the captured source; re-check quarterly, per Section 3.)** *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a freight-sector participant is itself eligible to become an ACCA Signatory, and what that would obligate the workspace to report, is not resolved in this brief and requires direct confirmation from the ACCA Community.

metadata.why_matters: Freight forwarders moving fine art for GCC-aligned galleries, museums, or any of the twelve named Art Fair Co-Commitment signatories are serving clients who have already committed to measured, reportable emissions reductions on a 2030 horizon. The newly launched Casi consultancy is actively building institutional carbon-auditing relationships, which is expected to surface a shipment-level Scope 3 data gap that no named consultant in the captured source currently fills from the freight side.

entries.body:
# 1. What's Moving and What Triggered It

MONITORING

[signal_event] The captured source states, verbatim: "This is the fifth in a series of climate plans released every four years by the city, as required by local law" *Source: NYC DEP mirror of "Mayor Adams Releases 'PlaNYC: Getting Sustainability Done'" press release. https://www.nyc.gov/site/dep/news/274-23/mayor-adams-releases-planyc-getting-sustainability-done-new-york-city-s-strategic-climate-plan*

New York City's Mayor's Office of Climate & Environmental Justice (MOCEJ) issued the plan under this recurring, legally mandated four-year cycle rather than as a one-off announcement. The captured source's own page heading states the release date, verbatim: "New York City's Strategic Climate Plan April 20, 2023" *Source: NYC DEP mirror of "Mayor Adams Releases 'PlaNYC: Getting Sustainability Done'" press release. https://www.nyc.gov/site/dep/news/274-23/mayor-adams-releases-planyc-getting-sustainability-done-new-york-city-s-strategic-climate-plan*

Two of the plan's own stated goals are directly relevant to freight and logistics operations inside New York City. The captured source states, verbatim: "Buildings are responsible for almost 70% of New York’s total greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, which is why we must improve our existing buildings while driving toward new low-carbon construction." *Source: PlaNYC: Getting Sustainability Done, Official MOCEJ Sub-page. https://www.nyc.gov/content/climate/pages/planyc-getting-sustainabilty-done* *Analytical inference:* a workspace leasing warehouse, depot, or staging space inside New York City sits inside the building stock this statistic frames as the city's largest single emissions source, which is the structural reason the plan's building-emissions goals (Section 3) matter to a tenant even though the stated obligation attaches to owners.

On transportation, the captured source states, verbatim: "We will cut transportation emissions in half by 2030 and ensure NYC’s streets provide a safe, clean, and livable environment" *Source: PlaNYC: Getting Sustainability Done, Official MOCEJ Sub-page. https://www.nyc.gov/content/climate/pages/planyc-getting-sustainabilty-done* The same source lists "Get polluting trucks off NYC streets" *Source: PlaNYC: Getting Sustainability Done, Official MOCEJ Sub-page. https://www.nyc.gov/content/climate/pages/planyc-getting-sustainabilty-done* among the transportation pillar's own stated sub-goals. *Operational implication:* this is the single most direct freight-relevant signal in the plan: a stated city goal to remove high-emission trucks from NYC streets, without (per the captured source) a specified vehicle-class threshold, zone boundary, or enforcement date.

# 2. Who's Driving It and What They Want

The item's own registered primary source states MOCEJ's mandate directly, verbatim: "We prepare New York City for the impacts of climate change and address remediation efforts from an equity and public health perspective." *Source: Mayor's Office of Climate & Environmental Justice, Homepage. https://nyc.gov/site/sustainability/index.page*

[driving_parties] The captured source names the driving executive and office, verbatim: "New York City Mayor Eric Adams today released PlaNYC: Getting Sustainability Done" *Source: NYC DEP mirror of "Mayor Adams Releases 'PlaNYC: Getting Sustainability Done'" press release. https://www.nyc.gov/site/dep/news/274-23/mayor-adams-releases-planyc-getting-sustainability-done-new-york-city-s-strategic-climate-plan*

[driving_parties] The plan was developed with input from a broad institutional apparatus. The captured source states, verbatim: "developed with input from the New York City Climate Cabinet, which consists of representatives from more than 35 city agencies and offices, the Sustainability Advisory Board , and stakeholders." *Source: NYC DEP mirror of "Mayor Adams Releases 'PlaNYC: Getting Sustainability Done'" press release. https://www.nyc.gov/site/dep/news/274-23/mayor-adams-releases-planyc-getting-sustainability-done-new-york-city-s-strategic-climate-plan*

[driving_parties] The captured source names the plan's own climate-dimension executive, verbatim: "New York City Chief Climate Officer and New York City Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) Commissioner Rohit T. Aggarwala" *Source: Mayor Adams Releases "PlaNYC: Getting Sustainability Done," NYC Mayor's Office Press Release, April 20, 2023. https://www.nyc.gov/office-of-the-mayor/news/274-23/mayor-adams-releases-planyc-getting-sustainability-done-new-york-city-s-strategic-climate-plan*

[driving_parties] MOCEJ Executive Director Kizzy Charles-Guzman is quoted directly in the captured source, verbatim: "This is a PlaNYC that threads public health, quality of life, and environmental justice throughout its initiatives and re-focuses climate work beyond decarbonization and adaptation" *Source: Mayor Adams Releases "PlaNYC: Getting Sustainability Done," NYC Mayor's Office Press Release, April 20, 2023. https://www.nyc.gov/office-of-the-mayor/news/274-23/mayor-adams-releases-planyc-getting-sustainability-done-new-york-city-s-strategic-climate-plan*

[driving_parties] Deputy Mayor for Operations Meera Joshi is quoted directly in the captured source on the plan's transportation-and-emissions dimension, verbatim: "Today, we are taking action to take polluting vehicles off our streets, offer more affordable renewable energy options, put our trash to work, and lower our emissions from every major source — buildings, transportation, and food." *Source: Mayor Adams Releases "PlaNYC: Getting Sustainability Done," NYC Mayor's Office Press Release, April 20, 2023. https://www.nyc.gov/office-of-the-mayor/news/274-23/mayor-adams-releases-planyc-getting-sustainability-done-new-york-city-s-strategic-climate-plan*

What the driving parties want, beyond the emissions goals themselves, is federal and state funding leverage. The captured source states, verbatim: "New York City contributes more to the federal and state governments than it typically receives in return, coupled with the unprecedented funding committed to climate action — in legislation such as the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, the Inflation Reduction Act, and the New York State Environmental Bond Act — several PlaNYC initiatives would benefit from federal and state grants." *Source: Mayor Adams Releases "PlaNYC: Getting Sustainability Done," NYC Mayor's Office Press Release, April 20, 2023. https://www.nyc.gov/office-of-the-mayor/news/274-23/mayor-adams-releases-planyc-getting-sustainability-done-new-york-city-s-strategic-climate-plan* The captured source further states, verbatim: "The city has therefore formed the New York City Federal Infrastructure Funding Task Force, which is working to maximize federal and state funding by helping select strong shovel-worthy and shovel-ready projects that meet the guidelines and standards of new and existing competitive grant opportunities." *Source: Mayor Adams Releases "PlaNYC: Getting Sustainability Done," NYC Mayor's Office Press Release, April 20, 2023. https://www.nyc.gov/office-of-the-mayor/news/274-23/mayor-adams-releases-planyc-getting-sustainability-done-new-york-city-s-strategic-climate-plan* *Analytical inference:* a plan this dependent on discretionary federal and state grant competition, rather than a dedicated appropriated budget line, carries execution-timeline risk for any of its sub-initiatives (including the transportation and buildings goals in Section 3) that the captured source does not itself resolve.

# 3. Expected Trajectory and Conversion Triggers

WINDOW CLOSING

[conversion_trigger] The captured source states the plan's own building-sector target, verbatim: "Support building owners in complying with Local Law 97 emissions reduction goals by 2030" *Source: PlaNYC: Getting Sustainability Done, Official MOCEJ Sub-page. https://www.nyc.gov/content/climate/pages/planyc-getting-sustainabilty-done*

[conversion_trigger] A second captured source states the specific numeric target behind that same 2030 goal, verbatim: "the city will continue to reduce emissions by helping large private buildings comply with Local Law 97, which aims to reduce the emissions produced by New York City’s largest buildings by 40 percent by 2030 and to be carbon-neutral by 2050." *Source: Mayor Adams Releases "PlaNYC: Getting Sustainability Done," NYC Mayor's Office Press Release, April 20, 2023. https://www.nyc.gov/office-of-the-mayor/news/274-23/mayor-adams-releases-planyc-getting-sustainability-done-new-york-city-s-strategic-climate-plan* *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any Local Law 97 compliance obligation applies to a commercial tenant, as opposed to exclusively the building owner, requires NYC legal counsel review of the specific lease terms against Local Law 97's own covered-building-owner provisions; this brief does not resolve that question.

Beyond buildings, the plan sets two longer-horizon citywide targets. The captured source states, verbatim: "equitably achieve net-zero emissions citywide by 2050" *Source: Mayor Adams Releases "PlaNYC: Getting Sustainability Done," NYC Mayor's Office Press Release, April 20, 2023. https://www.nyc.gov/office-of-the-mayor/news/274-23/mayor-adams-releases-planyc-getting-sustainability-done-new-york-city-s-strategic-climate-plan* and, on the city's own property portfolio, verbatim: "The city will install solar energy, electric building infrastructure, green roofs, and other renewable energy on all viable city-owned property by 2035." *Source: Mayor Adams Releases "PlaNYC: Getting Sustainability Done," NYC Mayor's Office Press Release, April 20, 2023. https://www.nyc.gov/office-of-the-mayor/news/274-23/mayor-adams-releases-planyc-getting-sustainability-done-new-york-city-s-strategic-climate-plan*

**Trajectory timeline.**
- 2030: Local Law 97 covered building owners must cut large-building emissions by 40 percent, and PlaNYC's own transportation goal is to cut citywide transportation emissions in half.
- 2035: all viable city-owned property is to carry solar energy and other clean infrastructure, per the captured source.
- 2050: the city's stated target is citywide net-zero emissions, with Local Law 97-covered buildings carbon-neutral by the same year.

*Analytical inference:* none of these three dates is itself a freight-specific compliance deadline; they are municipal targets whose downstream effect on a freight workspace (tenant cost pass-through, truck-access rulemaking, EV-charging infrastructure siting) is not yet specified in the captured source. The 2030 Local Law 97 date is the nearest and most consequential of the three for any workspace leasing NYC warehouse or depot space, which is why this section carries a WINDOW CLOSING label rather than plain MONITORING.

**An additional, undated conversion trigger.** The captured source states, verbatim: "The city will also phase out capital spending on new fossil fuel equipment and infrastructure and introduce a major citywide zoning text amendment — ‘City of Yes for Carbon Neutrality’ — which will remove obstacles to deploying clean energy, facilitate building retrofits for sustainability, and eliminate barriers to electrification." *Source: Mayor Adams Releases "PlaNYC: Getting Sustainability Done," NYC Mayor's Office Press Release, April 20, 2023. https://www.nyc.gov/office-of-the-mayor/news/274-23/mayor-adams-releases-planyc-getting-sustainability-done-new-york-city-s-strategic-climate-plan* *Specific enactment date and current status of the City of Yes for Carbon Neutrality zoning text amendment are not available from the captured source.*

# 4. Operational and Cost Implications If It Materializes

MONITORING

**Warehouse and depot leasing (buildings pillar).** *Operational implication:* a workspace leasing warehouse, depot, or staging space inside New York City sits inside the building stock the captured source frames as responsible for almost 70% of the city's GHG emissions (Section 1). Local Law 97 obligations fall on building owners rather than directly on the workspace as tenant, but lease structures commonly pass through capital-improvement costs to commercial tenants. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the workspace's own NYC lease terms create any direct or pass-through exposure to Local Law 97 compliance costs requires review of the lease itself against the statute; this brief does not perform that review.

**Road freight and last-mile delivery (transportation pillar).** *Operational implication:* the captured source's own stated sub-goal to "Get polluting trucks off NYC streets" *Source: PlaNYC: Getting Sustainability Done, Official MOCEJ Sub-page. https://www.nyc.gov/content/climate/pages/planyc-getting-sustainabilty-done* (Section 1) is the plan's most direct road-freight signal. If this goal is later translated into a specific vehicle-emissions-standard or zone-access restriction, workspaces running road freight or drayage into New York City would face compliance requirements on vehicle specification, routing, or both. The captured source does not itself specify a zone boundary, vehicle-class threshold, or enforcement date, so this remains a directional signal rather than an actionable requirement today.

**Fleet electrification.** *Operational implication:* the captured source's own transportation sub-goal, verbatim: "Help New Yorkers who must drive to drive electric" *Source: PlaNYC: Getting Sustainability Done, Official MOCEJ Sub-page. https://www.nyc.gov/content/climate/pages/planyc-getting-sustainabilty-done*, signals a citywide push toward vehicle electrification that extends to any last-mile or drayage fleet operating in New York City, ahead of a specific mandate.

*Specific cost figures for Local Law 97 tenant pass-through, truck-access compliance, or fleet electrification in the NYC context are not available from the captured source.*

# 5. Competitive Implications

MONITORING

**No named competitor positioning is available from the captured source pool.** Sourced competitor-specific claims are not emitted under the integrity rule; no freight forwarder, carrier, or logistics competitor is named anywhere in this item's captured text.

*Analytical inference:* a workspace that establishes NYC-compliant warehouse-leasing terms and documented awareness of the transportation pillar's truck-restriction direction, ahead of any formal zone enforcement, would be positioned ahead of a competitor that waits for regulatory finalization to start that conversation with NYC-based clients. This is a directional inference from the plan's own stated goals (Section 1, Section 3), not a claim about any specific competitor's current positioning.

# 6. Client Conversation Talking Points

**What the workspace can credibly say (grounded in the captured source):**

- New York City has a published, legally mandated strategic climate plan (PlaNYC), the fifth in a recurring four-year series, released April 20, 2023 under Mayor Eric Adams and MOCEJ (Section 1, Section 2).
- The plan states a citywide goal to cut transportation emissions in half by 2030 and to get polluting trucks off NYC streets, alongside a Local Law 97 goal to cut large-building emissions by 40 percent by 2030 and reach carbon-neutral by 2050 (Section 1, Section 3).
- The plan is explicitly dependent in part on federal and state grant funding rather than a dedicated appropriated budget line (Section 2).

**Questions worth posing to NYC-based clients:**

- Has your organization mapped its NYC facility or delivery operations against the plan's own stated goal to reduce polluting trucks on NYC streets, even though no specific zone or vehicle-class rule exists yet?
- Does your NYC warehouse or depot lease address who bears Local Law 97-related capital-improvement costs, owner or tenant?
- Is your sustainability reporting tracking New York City's own climate-budgeting initiative as a benchmark your NYC operations may eventually be compared against?

**Pitfalls to avoid:**

- Do not assert that a low-emission zone or specific truck-class restriction is currently in force in New York City; the captured source states only a directional 2030 transportation-emissions goal and a "Get polluting trucks off NYC streets" sub-goal, with no zone boundary, vehicle-class threshold, or enforcement date specified.
- Do not characterize PlaNYC itself as a binding regulatory instrument; it is a strategic plan. Local Law 97 is a separate, already-enacted instrument the plan references. *Legal Confirmation Required:* which PlaNYC sub-initiatives beyond Local Law 97 have been enacted into binding local law requires counsel review.
- Do not state that the City of Yes for Carbon Neutrality zoning text amendment has been enacted or has a specific effective date; the captured source announces it as a forthcoming initiative without an enactment date or status.

# 7. What the Workspace Should Do Now

MONITORING

[action_now] No specific, freight-directed action item is stated in the captured PlaNYC source text: the source addresses citywide sustainability goals and institutional funding strategy, not workspace-level compliance steps. The following actions are derived by the workspace from the plan's own stated goals (Section 1, Section 3), not quoted from the source.

**1. Confirm Local Law 97 exposure in any NYC warehouse or depot lease. (Monitoring, ahead of the plan's own 2030 target.)** *Operational implication:* request the lease's own capital-improvement and pass-through clauses now, rather than waiting for a 2030 compliance date that falls on the building owner by default.

**2. Track the transportation pillar's truck-restriction language for a future zone or vehicle-class rule.** *Operational implication:* the captured source states a goal, not yet a rule; re-check MOCEJ and NYC DOT rulemaking activity periodically rather than treating the 2030 target as an immediate operating constraint.

**3. Monitor the City of Yes for Carbon Neutrality zoning text amendment for an enactment date.** *Operational implication:* the captured source announces this as forthcoming without a date; a future enactment could affect on-site solar and EV-charging infrastructure options at any NYC-leased facility.

**4. Brief client-facing teams on the plan's own 2030 transportation and Local Law 97 targets.** *Operational implication:* clients with NYC operations, particularly in live events, film and TV production, and luxury goods, may reference this same plan in their own sustainability reporting; the workspace's own awareness of it is a low-cost, value-added talking point (Section 6).

# 8. Sources

| 3 | PlaNYC: Getting Sustainability Done, Official MOCEJ Sub-page | Binding/Government Initiative Page | https://www.nyc.gov/content/climate/pages/planyc-getting-sustainabilty-done | 2023 (current) |

entries.body:
# 1. What's Moving and What Triggered It

MONITORING

Two USGBC-driven scheduling events, dated within days of each other, reset the LEED v4-to-v5 transition calendar. The captured source states, verbatim: "USGBC has extended the LEED v4 and LEED v4.1 commercial registration close date from June 30, 2026 to June 30, 2027" *Source: LEED v4 and v4.1 commercial registration close extended to June 30, 2027, USGBC, May 27, 2026. https://www.usgbc.org/articles/leed-v4-and-v41-commercial-registration-close-extended-june-30-2027*

The stated reason is direct market feedback, not an internal USGBC decision made in isolation. The captured source states, verbatim: "USGBC members and project teams have shared that market conditions—including supply chain constraints, financing challenges and regulatory uncertainty—are affecting project timelines" *Source: LEED v4 and v4.1 commercial registration close extended to June 30, 2027, USGBC, May 27, 2026. https://www.usgbc.org/articles/leed-v4-and-v41-commercial-registration-close-extended-june-30-2027*

*Operational implication:* a one-year registration extension signals that a material share of the global LEED project pipeline is not moving at the pace USGBC originally projected, particularly in markets carrying supply-chain stress. For a workspace moving construction, fit-out, or building-systems freight, this extends the window during which LEED v4/v4.1 compliance documentation governs client procurement decisions, while simultaneously compressing the gap between today and the now-confirmed LEED v5 hard cutover.

The cutover itself is separately confirmed, on the USGBC Help Center. The captured source states, verbatim: "Starting on July 1, 2027*, LEED v5 will be the only version available for new registrations for the commercial LEED BD+C, ID+C, and O+M rating systems, with limited exceptions" *Source: LEED v5, USGBC Help Center, updated May 28, 2026. https://support.usgbc.org/hc/en-us/articles/25316160948755-LEED-v5*

The certification sunset date sits well beyond the cutover. The captured source states, verbatim: "Registration close 1 6/30/2027 Certification sunset 2 6/30/2033" *Source: LEED certification deadlines, U.S. Green Building Council. https://www.usgbc.org/tools/leed-certification/deadlines* This applies to every LEED v4 and v4.1 commercial rating system named on the deadlines page (BD+C, ID+C, O+M, and O+M Recertification).

LEED v5 is not merely announced; certification is already open. The captured source states, verbatim: "LEED v5 project registration is now available in Arc for the following rating systems: LEED v5 BD+C: New Construction LEED v5 BD+C: Core and Shell LEED v5 ID+C: Commercial Interiors LEED v5 O+M: Existing Buildings" *Source: LEED v5, USGBC Help Center, updated May 28, 2026. https://support.usgbc.org/hc/en-us/articles/25316160948755-LEED-v5*

A third, narrower track is moving in parallel. The captured source states, verbatim: "The second public comment period opened on May 14, 2026 and will close June 16, 2026" *Source: LEED v5, USGBC Help Center, updated May 28, 2026. https://support.usgbc.org/hc/en-us/articles/25316160948755-LEED-v5*

*Analytical inference:* the Cities rating system, covering municipal and district-scale projects, is running roughly one public-comment cycle behind the commercial BD+C/ID+C/O+M track, placing it on its own path toward ratification. A workspace serving urban infrastructure or large-scale mixed-use clients should monitor this track separately from the commercial track described above.

# 2. Who's Driving It and What They Want

**USGBC (U.S. Green Building Council)** is the standard-setting body and primary driver of both the extension and the cutover. The captured source states, verbatim: "LEED v5 ratified by members on March 28, 2025" *Source: LEED v5, USGBC Help Center, updated May 28, 2026. https://support.usgbc.org/hc/en-us/articles/25316160948755-LEED-v5* USGBC's own stated position is that "LEED v5 is USGBC’s recommended path for new projects, building on the strong foundation established by earlier versions of the rating system while raising the bar for measurable impact" *Source: LEED v4 and v4.1 commercial registration close extended to June 30, 2027, USGBC, May 27, 2026. https://www.usgbc.org/articles/leed-v4-and-v41-commercial-registration-close-extended-june-30-2027*

**The global LEED project community** exerted the pressure behind the registration extension. The captured source states, verbatim: "This decision reflects direct feedback from you, our global LEED community" *Source: LEED v4 and v4.1 commercial registration close extended to June 30, 2027, USGBC, May 27, 2026. https://www.usgbc.org/articles/leed-v4-and-v41-commercial-registration-close-extended-june-30-2027* *Analytical inference:* the extension was not a planned pause, it was a demand-driven concession, which suggests the transition is encountering real friction in the live project pipeline rather than proceeding on USGBC's original internal schedule.

**GBCI (Green Business Certification Inc.)** administers the parallel credentialing transition. The captured source states, verbatim: "As part of the transition from LEED v4 to LEED v5 , a limited-time beta exam period will be launched for both the LEED Green Associate and LEED AP with specialty credentials" *Source: LEED v5 beta exams to launch in 2026, GBCI, Jan. 29, 2026. https://www.gbci.org/leed-v5-beta-exams-launch-2026* Member ratification of a new LEED rating system version carries its own governance threshold: the captured source states, verbatim: "Member ratification requires a minimum of 50% of voting members supportive of adoption for the new version to continue towards market launch" *Source: LEED v5, USGBC Help Center, updated May 28, 2026. https://support.usgbc.org/hc/en-us/articles/25316160948755-LEED-v5*

**Platform and toolkit development** is continuing alongside the deadline changes. A source hosted on the Canada Green Building Council's (CAGBC) own site, there attributed to USGBC, states, verbatim: "This significant update marks a pivotal advancement in the LEED v5 journey, unlocking certification functionality and a suite of technical resources" *Source: LEED v5 expands: New Arc certification tools and resources for users, hosted on cagbc.org and there attributed to USGBC, November 3, 2025. https://www.cagbc.org/news-resources/cagbc-news/leed-v5-expands-new-arc-certification-tools-and-resources-for-users/* *Industry interpretation:* the same USGBC-authored content being republished on a national affiliate's own site indicates USGBC is actively coordinating international messaging on the transition timeline, not leaving individual national councils to interpret the deadlines independently.

# 3. Expected Trajectory and Conversion Triggers

WINDOW CLOSING

**Trajectory timeline.**
- March 28, 2025: LEED v5 ratified by members.
- April 28 to June 30, 2026: LEED Green Associate beta exam data-collection window.
- June 30 to Aug. 31, 2026: LEED AP with Specialty beta exam data-collection window.
- June 16, 2026: LEED v5 for Cities second public comment period closes.
- June 30, 2027: LEED v4 and LEED v4.1 commercial registration closes (extended from the original June 30, 2026 date).
- July 1, 2027: LEED v5 becomes the only version available for new commercial registrations (BD+C, ID+C, O+M), with limited exceptions.
- June 30, 2033: Certification sunset for all LEED v4 and v4.1 commercial rating systems.

**Beta credentialing window (near-term).** The captured source states, verbatim: "LEED Green Associate: April 28–June 30, 2026 LEED AP with Specialty: June 30–Aug. 31, 2026" *Source: LEED v5 beta exams to launch in 2026, GBCI, Jan. 29, 2026. https://www.gbci.org/leed-v5-beta-exams-launch-2026* During the data-collection phase, the captured source states, verbatim: "candidates are eligible for a 30% discount off standard exam pricing" *Source: LEED v5 beta exams to launch in 2026, GBCI, Jan. 29, 2026. https://www.gbci.org/leed-v5-beta-exams-launch-2026* *Operational implication:* commercial and client-facing staff already holding a v4 LEED Green Associate or LEED AP credential have a discounted, time-boxed entry point to v5 content fluency before the standard exam launches, relevant for any role that will field LEED v5 questions from clients between now and the July 1, 2027 cutover.

**Final exam publication.** The captured source states, verbatim: "The final version of the LEED v5 exams will debut after the results of the beta period have been analyzed" *Source: LEED v5 beta exams to launch in 2026, GBCI, Jan. 29, 2026. https://www.gbci.org/leed-v5-beta-exams-launch-2026* The captured source further states, verbatim: "the beta exam will remain available until the final exam is published, toward the end of 2026" *Source: LEED v5 beta exams to launch in 2026, GBCI, Jan. 29, 2026. https://www.gbci.org/leed-v5-beta-exams-launch-2026* *Analytical inference:* a credentialed v5 professional workforce only begins forming after this publication, meaning specification-writers producing LEED v5 procurement language before then are working from provisional, not final, exam-validated content.

**Toolkit and reporting roadmap (2026).** The captured source states, verbatim: "In 2026, project teams can expect even more growth: Additional Project Priority credits Expanded international guidance and alternative compliance paths Regular addenda updates Project impact reports" *Source: LEED v5 expands: New Arc certification tools and resources for users, hosted on cagbc.org and there attributed to USGBC, November 3, 2025. https://www.cagbc.org/news-resources/cagbc-news/leed-v5-expands-new-arc-certification-tools-and-resources-for-users/* Of these, the most operationally relevant to a freight-forwarding workspace is the project impact report. The captured source states, verbatim: "Project impact reports: These reports will summarize certifications using metrics on emissions, energy, water, waste, IAQ, transportation and resilience, strengthening project transparency and stakeholder communication" *Source: LEED v5 expands: New Arc certification tools and resources for users, hosted on cagbc.org and there attributed to USGBC, November 3, 2025. https://www.cagbc.org/news-resources/cagbc-news/leed-v5-expands-new-arc-certification-tools-and-resources-for-users/*

**Conversion trigger 1: the July 1, 2027 hard cutover.** The captured source states, verbatim: "Starting on July 1, 2027*, LEED v5 will be the only version available for new registrations for the commercial LEED BD+C, ID+C, and O+M rating systems, with limited exceptions" *Source: LEED v5, USGBC Help Center, updated May 28, 2026. https://support.usgbc.org/hc/en-us/articles/25316160948755-LEED-v5* *Analytical inference:* after this date, any client beginning a new commercial LEED project enters exclusively under v5, and procurement specifications for materials, components, and logistics services will increasingly reference v5 credit documentation rather than v4/v4.1.

**Conversion trigger 2: the June 30, 2027/June 30, 2033 registration-and-sunset pair.** The captured source states, verbatim: "Registration close 1 6/30/2027 Certification sunset 2 6/30/2033" *Source: LEED certification deadlines, U.S. Green Building Council. https://www.usgbc.org/tools/leed-certification/deadlines* *Operational implication:* a client registering a project under v4/v4.1 before June 30, 2027 retains until June 30, 2033 to complete certification, so the workspace will be serving v4, v4.1, and v5 documentation requirements simultaneously across its client base for the full length of that window, not a brief transition month.

*Specific v5-for-Cities ratification timing is not available from these captured sources as of the export date. Only the June 16, 2026 second-comment-period close date above is confirmed; the ratification date that follows it has not been published.*

# 4. Operational and Cost Implications If It Materializes

MONITORING

*Operational implication:* LEED itself imposes no direct requirement on a freight forwarder. LEED certifies buildings and projects, not vendors or supply-chain services. The operational exposure runs through the workspace's clients' own certification obligations, specifically the data those clients will need to source FROM their logistics providers.

**Project impact reporting (the direct link to freight data).** The captured source states, verbatim: "Project impact reports: These reports will summarize certifications using metrics on emissions, energy, water, waste, IAQ, transportation and resilience, strengthening project transparency and stakeholder communication" *Source: LEED v5 expands: New Arc certification tools and resources for users, hosted on cagbc.org and there attributed to USGBC, November 3, 2025. https://www.cagbc.org/news-resources/cagbc-news/leed-v5-expands-new-arc-certification-tools-and-resources-for-users/* *Analytical inference:* a client pursuing LEED v5 certification whose project impact report covers transportation will need transport-related data (mode, distance, carrier, and associated emissions) from somewhere in its supply chain, and a freight forwarder handling that project's material or equipment movements is a plausible data source the client's project team may approach. The specific data format or level of granularity USGBC will require is not stated in these captured sources.

**Dual-track documentation burden through 2033.** As Section 3 states, a project registered under v4 or v4.1 before June 30, 2027 has until June 30, 2033 to certify. *Operational implication:* the workspace should expect to support both LEED v4/v4.1-era documentation conventions and LEED v5's new reporting elements concurrently for roughly six years, not a short overlap window.

# 5. Competitive Implications

MONITORING

*No sourced competitor-specific positioning data is available in these source blocks.* No source in this item's captured pool names a specific competing freight forwarder's positioning on LEED v5 transport documentation or emissions-data readiness; the pool corroborates the USGBC/GBCI transition signal itself but not named-competitor freight positioning.

*Analytical inference:* a workspace that builds transport-data capture and reporting capability ahead of client demand, before LEED v5 project impact reports covering transportation become common on client procurement requests, is positioned to respond when clients begin asking; a workspace that waits for the request is not.

*Industry interpretation:* USGBC's own coordinated messaging across its Help Center, its main articles feed, and a national affiliate's site (Section 2) suggests the LEED v5 transition is being treated as a major platform event rather than a routine version bump, which increases the likelihood that client-facing sustainability and procurement teams will be actively asking their vendors about it well before the July 1, 2027 cutover.

# 6. Client Conversation Talking Points

**What the workspace can credibly say:**

- LEED v4 and v4.1 commercial registration has been extended by one year, from June 30, 2026 to June 30, 2027. Clients with projects already in motion under v4/v4.1 have additional runway (Section 1).
- LEED v5 is live for new commercial registrations now, in Arc, for BD+C, ID+C, and O+M (Section 1).
- The certification sunset for v4/v4.1 is June 30, 2033. A project registered before July 1, 2027 has until mid-2033 to complete certification (Section 3).
- USGBC's own 2026 roadmap includes project impact reports covering transportation as a tracked metric alongside emissions, energy, water, waste, IAQ, and resilience (Section 3, Section 4).

**Questions the workspace can pose to clients:**

- Is your project registered under LEED v4, LEED v4.1, or LEED v5? This determines which documentation window and deadline pair applies.
- Will your project team be producing a LEED v5 project impact report, and if so, has your team identified how it will source transportation data for that report?
- Are your LEED consultants already credentialed under the v5 beta program, or are they still working from v4 credential content?

**Claims to avoid:**

- Do not assert that LEED v5 has published a specific logistics or freight emissions documentation format for vendors; these captured sources confirm transportation is a tracked metric in project impact reports, not that a specific vendor-facing data format exists yet.
- Do not represent the workspace itself as "LEED v5 compliant". LEED certification is a project-level designation, not a vendor designation.
- Do not cite a ratification date for LEED v5 for Cities; only the second public comment period's close date (June 16, 2026) is confirmed in these sources.

# 7. What the Workspace Should Do Now

ACTION REQUIRED

**1. Build a simple client-project LEED version register.** Identify LEED-active clients and record, per project, whether it runs under v4, v4.1, or v5, and which registration and sunset deadlines apply. This is zero-cost intelligence that directly informs documentation and account-planning priorities through the multi-year overlap window described in Section 4.

**2. Follow USGBC's own next-step guidance for LEED-active clients.** [action_now] The captured source states, verbatim: "Ready for LEED v5? Register new projects via the Arc platform" *Source: LEED v4 and v4.1 commercial registration close extended to June 30, 2027, USGBC, May 27, 2026. https://www.usgbc.org/articles/leed-v4-and-v41-commercial-registration-close-extended-june-30-2027* For clients already committed to v4 or v4.1, the captured source separately states, verbatim: "Intending to certify under LEED v4 or LEED v4.1? Register your LEED BD+C, ID+C and O+M projects by June 30, 2027" *Source: LEED v4 and v4.1 commercial registration close extended to June 30, 2027, USGBC, May 27, 2026. https://www.usgbc.org/articles/leed-v4-and-v41-commercial-registration-close-extended-june-30-2027* *Operational implication:* knowing which of these two paths each client project is on determines which deadline (Section 3) the workspace should be tracking on that account.

**3. Put transportation-data capture for LEED v5 project impact reports on the emissions-reporting roadmap.** *Operational implication:* the direction of travel is sourced (Section 3, Section 4) even though the specific data format is not yet published; the workspace's own transport-emissions data capability should be positioned as ready before clients start asking, with July 1, 2027 as a reasonable target readiness date.

**4. Monitor the LEED v5 for Cities track separately.** Re-check after June 16, 2026 for USGBC's publication of next steps following the second public comment period (Section 1, Section 3); this track is on its own schedule from the commercial BD+C/ID+C/O+M track and should not be assumed to follow the same July 1, 2027 cutover.

**Re-check window:** this brief should be refreshed after June 16, 2026, to capture the outcome of the LEED v5 for Cities second public comment period, and again as the final v5 credentialing exams are published toward the end of 2026 (Section 3).

# 8. Sources
