entries.body:
# 1. What's Moving and What Triggered It

MONITORING

The captured WEF press release states, verbatim: "Davos-Klosters, Switzerland, 16 January 2024 – The First Movers Coalition (FMC), a global public-private partnership by the World Economic Forum and the United States government working to decarbonize the world’s heavy-emitting sectors, now represents the world’s largest private sector demand signal for emerging climate technologies with more than 120 commitments from 96 members, the Forum announces today." *Source: World Economic Forum press release, 16 January 2024. https://www.weforum.org/press/2024/01/wef24-first-movers-coalition-commitments/*

Two years earlier, the coalition's own membership base was a fraction of its January 2024 size. The captured source states, verbatim: "From 35 members when FMC was launched at COP26, the coalition has now reached 96 members and includes some of the world’s largest companies." *Source: World Economic Forum press release, 16 January 2024. https://www.weforum.org/press/2024/01/wef24-first-movers-coalition-commitments/*

The captured AFSA source states the coalition's founding context, verbatim: "President Joe Biden and the World Economic Forum launched the First Movers Coalition (FMC) at the United Nations Climate Change Conference in Glasgow (COP26) in November 2021. The launch was supported by 35 global companies that joined to send a powerful signal that there is firm market demand for the emerging technologies essential for a net-zero transition in “hard-to-abate” sectors." *Source: American Foreign Service Association / Foreign Service Journal, September 2024. https://afsa.org/decarbonizing-industry-through-demand-first-movers-coalition*

A second signal event followed two years later: the WEF's own publication line reads, verbatim: "Published : 19 January 2026" and the same source states, verbatim: "This impact report highlights how First Movers Coalition (FMC) members are delivering on their net-zero commitments within a complex global market. It showcases the successful approaches, emerging trends and concrete solutions that demonstrate how coordinated corporate demand can help shape a net-zero economy." *Source: World Economic Forum, First Movers Coalition Impact Brief 2026, published 19 January 2026. https://www.weforum.org/publications/first-movers-coalition-impact-brief-2026/*

*Analytical inference:* the January 2026 Impact Brief is itself a signal, not merely a status update: the World Economic Forum publishing a dedicated impact report on member delivery indicates the coalition has moved from a launch-and-announce posture (2021 to 2024) into an accountability posture where member commitments are being tracked against actual offtake and procurement outcomes.

# 2. Who's Driving It and What They Want

The captured WEF press release names the most recently joined member companies, verbatim: "The most recent members to join FMC are: Qatar Airways, Velux, The Coca Cola Company, GE Vernova, DP World Limited, Capgemini, Danfoss A/S, Hanwha Ocean, Neutron Holdings (Lime), Volvo Cars, Inc., Chooose AS, Boom Technology, Drax Corporate Limited and Norsk Hydro ASA" *Source: World Economic Forum press release, 16 January 2024. https://www.weforum.org/press/2024/01/wef24-first-movers-coalition-commitments/*

The captured AFSA source names the coalition's co-chair, verbatim: "Former U.S. Special Presidential Envoy for Climate John Kerry became co-chair of the coalition and continues to drive this initiative forward, rallying top companies with high climate ambition and a willingness to harness their purchasing power to decarbonize heavy-emitting industries." *Source: American Foreign Service Association / Foreign Service Journal, September 2024. https://afsa.org/decarbonizing-industry-through-demand-first-movers-coalition*

Named party Børge Brende, President of the World Economic Forum, is quoted directly in the captured press release: "“The First Movers Coalition is proving the power of private sector cooperation to drive meaningful climate action,” says Børge Brende, President, World Economic Forum. “Together, FMC’s member companies are sending an unprecedented signal of demand, which will serve to drive up investment in and production of the critical emerging technologies needed to decarbonize the most heavy-emitting industrial sectors”." *Source: World Economic Forum press release, 16 January 2024. https://www.weforum.org/press/2024/01/wef24-first-movers-coalition-commitments/*

Named party John Kerry, US Special Presidential Envoy for Climate, is quoted directly in the same captured source: "“The First Movers Coalition is driving critical progress in the some of the hardest to address sectors,” said John Kerry, US Special Presidential Envoy for Climate. “As members participate in offtake agreements and invest in decarbonization projects in support of their FMC commitments, they continue to give confidence to this market to develop faster. This approach is pivotal in expanding the use and availability of the breakthrough technological solutions that will enable the deep decarbonization of heavy-emitting sectors.”" *Source: World Economic Forum press release, 16 January 2024. https://www.weforum.org/press/2024/01/wef24-first-movers-coalition-commitments/*

*Industry interpretation:* both named quotes frame FMC membership as a demand-aggregation strategy rather than a compliance obligation. Member companies are named individuals and named corporations exercising purchasing power voluntarily, not regulators imposing a requirement, which shapes how this signal should be discussed with clients (Section 6).

**Two named members with direct freight-sector relevance.** The captured AFSA source states, verbatim: "In shipping, Amazon, a founding member of the FMC, has been instrumental in getting the Zero Emission Maritime Buyers Alliance (ZEMBA) off the ground." *Source: American Foreign Service Association / Foreign Service Journal, September 2024. https://afsa.org/decarbonizing-industry-through-demand-first-movers-coalition* The same source states, verbatim: "Microsoft is leading the charge, accounting for more than 60 percent of all engineered CDR purchases made to date." *Source: American Foreign Service Association / Foreign Service Journal, September 2024. https://afsa.org/decarbonizing-industry-through-demand-first-movers-coalition*

*Analytical inference:* Amazon's role as a founding member driving ZEMBA and Microsoft's dominant position in carbon dioxide removal purchases are two distinct examples of the same mechanism: a single large buyer using FMC membership to aggregate demand in one sector. For freight forwarders, the Amazon and ZEMBA example is the more directly relevant of the two, since it acts on ocean freight capacity itself rather than a carbon-credit market adjacent to freight.

**The purchasing-commitment mechanism.** The captured AFSA source states, verbatim: "Members make purchasing commitments applicable to a minimum percentage of their existing spend on products and services in one or more FMC sectors by 2030 (e.g., 10 percent of the company’s steel procured or 10 percent of the volume of goods shipped overseas)." *Source: American Foreign Service Association / Foreign Service Journal, September 2024. https://afsa.org/decarbonizing-industry-through-demand-first-movers-coalition*

# 3. Expected Trajectory and Conversion Triggers

WINDOW CLOSING

**Trajectory timeline.**
- November 2021: First Movers Coalition launched at COP26 in Glasgow, supported by 35 global founding companies.
- 16 January 2024: FMC reaches 96 members with more than 120 commitments and an estimated $16 billion annual demand target by 2030.
- 19 January 2026: World Economic Forum publishes the First Movers Coalition Impact Brief 2026, documenting member delivery against commitments.

**The 2030 to 2050 scale target.** The captured WEF press release states, verbatim: "By 2030, these commitments will represent an estimated annual demand of $16 billion for emerging climate technologies and 31 million tonnes (Mt) CO2e in annual emissions reductions." *Source: World Economic Forum press release, 16 January 2024. https://www.weforum.org/press/2024/01/wef24-first-movers-coalition-commitments/*

**Conversion trigger 1 - the stated technology rationale.** The captured WEF press release states, verbatim: "Half of the emissions reductions needed by 2050 must come from technologies not yet available at scale, so creating demand for these technologies will be essential to kickstart the market and catalyse their commercial adoption." *Source: World Economic Forum press release, 16 January 2024. https://www.weforum.org/press/2024/01/wef24-first-movers-coalition-commitments/* *Analytical inference:* this is the coalition's own stated theory of change: because half of 2050's needed emissions reductions depend on technologies not yet commercially available, the coalition's purpose is to convert voluntary purchasing signals into the guaranteed early demand that de-risks investment in those technologies. The point at which this converts into freight-relevant pressure is when a member embeds an FMC-aligned threshold into its own procurement or shipping contracts (see Amazon/ZEMBA below).

**Conversion trigger 2 - offtake activity already underway.** The captured WEF press release states, verbatim: "As of today, FMC members have been involved in 94 offtake agreements or investment projects to secure emerging climate technologies and near-zero emission goods and services from qualified suppliers." *Source: World Economic Forum press release, 16 January 2024. https://www.weforum.org/press/2024/01/wef24-first-movers-coalition-commitments/* This is not a future trigger; it is evidence the voluntary signal is already converting into contracted supply relationships.

**Conversion trigger 3 - a concrete, freight-relevant offtake in ocean shipping.** The captured AFSA source states, verbatim: "Amazon is supporting joint efforts under ZEMBA to ship 600,000 TEUs (20-foot equivalent units) on zero-emission vessels over three years, which will result in close to 1 million tons of CO2 emissions reduction." *Source: American Foreign Service Association / Foreign Service Journal, September 2024. https://afsa.org/decarbonizing-industry-through-demand-first-movers-coalition* *Operational implication:* this is the single clearest example in the captured pool of an FMC commitment converting directly into an ocean-freight capacity decision. When an anchor shipper of Amazon's scale block-books zero-emission vessel capacity through a buyers' alliance, carriers without compliant tonnage are excluded from that specific freight, and forwarders without carrier access to compliant capacity face the same exclusion downstream.

**Structural pressure behind the trigger.** The captured AFSA source states, verbatim: "The window is rapidly closing to demonstrate and commercialize these innovative technologies over the critical 2020s decade, so they become available for massive scale-up to enable net-zero emissions by 2050." *Source: American Foreign Service Association / Foreign Service Journal, September 2024. https://afsa.org/decarbonizing-industry-through-demand-first-movers-coalition* The same source states, verbatim: "The Mission Possible Partnership’s Global Project Tracker reveals, however, that the heavy industry transition needs to accelerate sevenfold to meet 2030 climate targets." *Source: American Foreign Service Association / Foreign Service Journal, September 2024. https://afsa.org/decarbonizing-industry-through-demand-first-movers-coalition* *Analytical inference:* a sevenfold acceleration gap combined with a closing commercialisation window indicates the constraint through the rest of this decade is available near-zero supply, not buyer demand, which is a different competitive dynamic than a typical regulatory-compliance market.

**Sector demand growth underlying the trajectory.** The captured AFSA source states, verbatim: "If left unabated, these sectors are projected to account for 50 percent of emissions by 2050, driven by a significant increase in global demand estimated at 80 percent for aluminum, 40 percent for cement and concrete, and 30 percent for steel." *Source: American Foreign Service Association / Foreign Service Journal, September 2024. https://afsa.org/decarbonizing-industry-through-demand-first-movers-coalition* The same source states, verbatim: "While sea freight is predicted to triple, trucking is expected to double by mid-century." *Source: American Foreign Service Association / Foreign Service Journal, September 2024. https://afsa.org/decarbonizing-industry-through-demand-first-movers-coalition* *Operational implication:* sea freight volume tripling and trucking volume doubling by mid-century, layered onto the six hard-to-abate sectors' own emissions growth, is itself a forward demand signal for near-zero transport capacity across all three of the workspace's primary and secondary modes, independent of whether a given client is an FMC member.

# 4. Operational and Cost Implications If It Materializes

COST ALERT

**Air (primary mode for time-critical verticals).** *Operational implication:* for live events, fine art, film and TV, and luxury goods clients moving high-value or time-critical cargo, FMC-driven demand for sustainable aviation fuel translates into a cost premium the workspace should be ready to discuss. The captured AFSA source states, verbatim: "sustainable aviation fuel can cost five times more than traditional jet fuels." *Source: American Foreign Service Association / Foreign Service Journal, September 2024. https://afsa.org/decarbonizing-industry-through-demand-first-movers-coalition* At a five-times premium, this is a material line item on any air freight quote where a client requests or requires SAF-blended fuel.

**Ocean (secondary mode, directly affected by the ZEMBA example above).** *Operational implication:* the captured AFSA source states, verbatim: "zero-emission fuels for shipping currently cost three to four times the price of bunker fuel" *Source: American Foreign Service Association / Foreign Service Journal, September 2024. https://afsa.org/decarbonizing-industry-through-demand-first-movers-coalition* Combined with the ZEMBA 600,000 TEU commitment described in Section 3, this indicates both a cost premium on compliant ocean capacity and a volume of capacity being pre-purchased by large FMC-aligned shippers, tightening spot availability for non-members on the same lanes.

**Road and rail.** *Specific current cost differential for FMC-compliant zero-emission trucking or rail is not available from the captured source set.* The trucking demand-growth figure in Section 3 (trucking volume expected to double by mid-century) is a volume signal, not a cost signal, for this mode.

# 5. Competitive Implications

COMPETITIVE EDGE

**The First Suppliers Hub as a procurement filter.** The captured WEF press release states, verbatim: "The FMC launched the First Suppliers Hub , a global repository of innovative and emerging technologies and suppliers that are working to meet the FMC commitment thresholds across several key high-emissions sectors. The hub features more than 80 decarbonization efforts that are currently underway" *Source: World Economic Forum press release, 16 January 2024. https://www.weforum.org/press/2024/01/wef24-first-movers-coalition-commitments/* *Analytical inference:* the First Suppliers Hub functions as a preferred-supplier directory for FMC buyer members. Freight and logistics operators, whether carriers, forwarders, or NVOCCs, whose services are not listed or who cannot demonstrate alignment with FMC commitment thresholds are less visible to this buyer cohort's own procurement process than suppliers who are listed.

**Named logistics-sector members.** DP World Limited and Hanwha Ocean appear among the named companies in Section 2's member list, both logistics and maritime infrastructure companies rather than cargo-owner principals. *Industry interpretation:* their FMC membership signals the coalition's influence is reaching port, terminal, and shipbuilding capacity layers of the freight sector, not only the cargo-owner side; a workspace competing for business connected to either company should account for their own stated FMC alignment.

**Named freight-forwarder competitor positioning.** No source in this item's captured pool names a specific competing freight forwarder's positioning relative to First Movers Coalition membership or the First Suppliers Hub; this brief does not invent that data to appear complete.

# 6. Client Conversation Talking Points

**What the workspace can credibly say:**

- FMC represents a large, named private-sector demand signal, with 96 members and more than 120 commitments as of 16 January 2024, targeting an estimated $16 billion in annual demand by 2030 (Section 1, Section 3).
- Amazon, a founding FMC member, is directly driving ocean-freight decarbonization through ZEMBA, having committed to ship 600,000 TEUs on zero-emission vessels over three years (Section 2, Section 3).
- Sustainable aviation fuel and zero-emission shipping fuel both carry a real, sourced cost premium today (five times and three-to-four times respectively) that should be discussed with any client requesting near-zero-emission transport (Section 4).

**What to avoid:**

- Do not present FMC membership as a regulatory compliance requirement. It is a voluntary coalition of member companies making purchasing commitments. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether an FMC member's own procurement commitments, once embedded in a supply or freight contract, create binding obligations on the workspace as a contracted carrier or forwarder requires contract-specific legal review; this brief does not resolve that question.
- Do not cite the $16 billion annual demand figure as confirmed current spend; the captured source describes it as an estimate of what commitments "will represent" by 2030.
- Do not claim the workspace's own operations are FMC-aligned without being able to identify the specific FMC commitment threshold that applies to a given client and evidence that the workspace's own carrier or supplier relationships meet it.

**Questions to pose to clients:**

- Has your company made FMC purchasing commitments in aviation, shipping, or another covered sector, and what percentage threshold applies by 2030?
- Are you currently procuring SAF-blended air freight or zero-emission ocean capacity to fulfil that commitment, and does your budget already reflect the current cost premium?
- Does your procurement team require emissions documentation from freight providers such as the workspace to count shipments toward your FMC commitment?

# 7. What the Workspace Should Do Now

ACTION REQUIRED

**1. Track the Impact Brief 2026 for member delivery data.** [action_now] The captured WEF Impact Brief 2026 landing page confirms active monitoring of member delivery against commitments, verbatim: "This impact report highlights how First Movers Coalition (FMC) members are delivering on their net-zero commitments within a complex global market." *Source: World Economic Forum, First Movers Coalition Impact Brief 2026, published 19 January 2026. https://www.weforum.org/publications/first-movers-coalition-impact-brief-2026/* The captured pool carries only this landing page's abstract, not the full report body; when the full report becomes available in the captured corpus, it becomes the primary source for updated offtake data and sector-by-sector progress.

**2. Map carrier and supplier relationships against FMC-adjacent capacity.** *Operational implication:* identify which of the workspace's primary air and ocean carriers participate in FMC, ZEMBA, or an equivalent near-zero capacity programme; carriers with FMC-aligned capacity can be presented to clients with FMC commitments as compliant options.

**3. Prepare a SAF and zero-emission-fuel cost scenario for client pricing conversations.** *Operational implication:* the five-times SAF premium and the three-to-four-times zero-emission shipping fuel premium (Section 4) are publicly sourced figures the workspace can use to prepare a cost scenario in advance of a client request, rather than reacting to one.

**4. Monitor ZEMBA capacity allocation on affected ocean lanes.** *Operational implication:* for the workspace's own ocean freight activity, assess whether lanes used by the workspace intersect with lanes where ZEMBA co-buyers concentrate their zero-emission vessel bookings, and whether spot or contract capacity access on those lanes is affected by the scarcity this creates.

**5. Re-check the Impact Brief's full body and the coalition's Davos cadence for the next annual update.** *Operational implication:* the January 2026 Impact Brief is the most recent publication available in the captured pool; given the coalition's prior pattern of major announcements at the WEF Annual Meeting, set a monitor to re-pull coverage around the next Annual Meeting cycle.

# 8. Sources

| # | Title | Type | Publisher | Date | URL |
|---|-------|------|-----------|------|-----|
| 1 | First Movers Coalition: 120 Commitments for Breakthrough Industrial Decarbonization Technologies | Press Release | World Economic Forum | 16 January 2024 | https://www.weforum.org/press/2024/01/wef24-first-movers-coalition-commitments/ |
| 2 | Decarbonizing Industry Through Demand: The First Movers Coalition | Industry/Policy Analysis | American Foreign Service Association / Foreign Service Journal | September 2024 | https://afsa.org/decarbonizing-industry-through-demand-first-movers-coalition |
| 3 | First Movers Coalition Impact Brief 2026 | Institutional Publication | World Economic Forum | 19 January 2026 | https://www.weforum.org/publications/first-movers-coalition-impact-brief-2026/ |

*Note: four additional captures in this item's pool did not ground any claim in this brief. Two WEF domain pages (weforum.org/first-movers-coalition and initiatives.weforum.org/first-movers-coalition/home) returned only cookie-consent and navigation content, not FMC page text. The BCG source (bcg.com/publications/2023/harnessing-purchasing-power-drive-deep-decarbonization-first-movers-coalition) returned only BCG site navigation and service-menu content, not the article body. A WTO capture (wto.org/english/tratop_e/envir_e/envir_e.htm) returned real page text, but it is the WTO's general Trade and Environment landing page, not the WEF/WTO TESSD First Movers Coalition presentation the item's title references, and it contains no First Movers Coalition content; it is listed here for registry completeness but grounds nothing in this brief.*

metadata.what_is_it: A market intelligence signal on the World Economic Forum's First Movers Coalition (FMC), a voluntary public-private demand-aggregation coalition of 96 member companies that had made more than 120 purchasing commitments toward near-zero emission goods and services by 2030 as of a 16 January 2024 WEF press release, with a January 2026 WEF Impact Brief now tracking member delivery against those commitments.

entries.body:
# 1. What's Moving and What Triggered It

MONITORING

The Zero Emission Maritime Buyers Alliance (ZEMBA) is a first-of-its-kind buyers group working to accelerate the most sustainable, scalable, and economically viable solutions for the maritime sector. *Source: ZEMBA Official Website (shipzemba.org), captured 2026. https://www.shipzemba.org/*

The triggering condition is a structural market failure stated by ZEMBA's own secretariat: "99% of vessels on the water today operate on high-emission fuels." *Source: ZEMBA Official Website (shipzemba.org), captured 2026. https://www.shipzemba.org/* *Analytical inference:* when no single cargo buyer commands enough freight volume to move the carrier market alone, an aggregated buyers' coalition is the mechanism that concentrates offtake signals to a scale carriers can finance against.

The alliance's own launch statement, dated March 9, 2023: "the mission of ZEMBA is to enable companies to access zero-emission shipping solutions that are not currently available.  March 9, 2023 Through ZEMBA, climate-leading cargo owners create the first competitive process for forward procuring zero-emission maritime freight services." *Source: The Aspen Institute, March 9, 2023. https://aspeninstitute.org/news/zero-emission-maritime-buyers-alliance-launch*

Two competitive tender rounds have since completed (Section 3), moving ZEMBA from a launch announcement into a live procurement instrument with dated, on-water deployment commitments.

Prize Nominee  March 19, 2026 "ZEMBA is deeply honored to announce that it has been named a 2026 Earthshot Prize..." *Source: ZEMBA Official Website (shipzemba.org), captured 2026. https://www.shipzemba.org/* *Analytical inference:* an Earthshot Prize nomination is a mainstream sustainability-credibility signal; it raises ZEMBA's visibility with corporate sustainability and procurement teams, which could accelerate membership growth beyond the 45+ companies already participating (Section 2).

*Operational implication:* for workspaces whose clients operate ocean-dependent supply chains, particularly those with named ZEMBA members among their own customers or peers, the alliance's shift from launch announcement to two completed, carrier-committed tenders changes this from a signal to monitor into a live commercial fact to route around.

# 2. Who's Driving It and What They Want

**Founding and secretariat.** the Aspen Institute was pleased to announce the formation of the Zero Emission Maritime Buyers Alliance (ZEMBA), alongside co-founders Amazon, Patagonia, and Tchibo. *Source: The Aspen Institute, March 9, 2023. https://aspeninstitute.org/news/zero-emission-maritime-buyers-alliance-launch* Named party Dan Porterfield, President and CEO of the Aspen Institute, is quoted directly on the founding members' role: "The Aspen Institute is inspired by industry leaders like Amazon, Patagonia, and Tchibo who are advancing solutions that will help us achieve full maritime decarbonization,” said Dan Porterfield, President and CEO of the Aspen Institute," *Source: The Aspen Institute, March 9, 2023. https://aspeninstitute.org/news/zero-emission-maritime-buyers-alliance-launch*

**Cargo owner members (demand side).** The captured second-tender source names the participating member companies beyond the three founders, verbatim: "including cofounders Amazon, Patagonia and Tchibo, and members including Beiersdorf, Brooks Running, Green Worldwide Shipping, IKEA, Nike, Poly Medicure Ltd., and Sport-Thieme" *Source: The Aspen Institute, ZEMBA Second Tender Winners, December 17, 2025. https://www.aspeninstitute.org/news/zemba-second-tender-winners/* Their own stated interest, per the captured ZEMBA source: "credibly reduce your company’s Scope 3 emissions, and lower long-term costs of the clean energy transition by channeling investment toward the most scalable fuels and technologies." *Source: ZEMBA Official Website (shipzemba.org), captured 2026. https://www.shipzemba.org/*

The captured Hapag-Lloyd source independently states the current scale of membership: "The ZEMBA is a non-profit buyer’s group within the maritime sector, currently comprising over 45 members, including international heavyweights like Amazon, IKEA, and Nike. It aims to accelerate commercial zero-emission shipping, enable economies of scale, and help cargo owners maximize emissions reduction potential beyond what any one buyer could" *Source: Hapag-Lloyd Press Release, December 17, 2025. https://www.hapag-lloyd.com/en/company/press/releases/2025/12/hapag-lloyd-wins-zemba-s-second-tender-for-pioneering-e-fuel-dep.html* *Analytical inference:* Amazon, IKEA, and Nike are named as members by two independent captured sources (Aspen Institute and Hapag-Lloyd), which corroborates their participation above single-source status.

**Winning carrier (supply side).** Hapag-Lloyd, one of the world’s leading container shipping companies, was selected as the winner of ZEMBA’s inaugural tender. *Source: The Aspen Institute, Inaugural ZEMBA Tender Completion, 2024. https://www.aspeninstitute.org/news/zemba-inaugural-tender-2024/* Hapag-Lloyd has since won ZEMBA's second tender as well (Section 3); the carrier's own stated interest, quoted directly from its CEO: "Deploying e-methanol is an essential step in our journey to reach net-zero fleet operations by 2045. We are very grateful for the trust that all ZEMBA members have placed in our capabilities, and we remain fully committed to reducing greenhouse gas emissions and contributing to a greener future for global shipping,” said Rolf Habben Jansen, CEO of Hapag-Lloyd." *Source: Hapag-Lloyd Press Release, December 17, 2025. https://www.hapag-lloyd.com/en/company/press/releases/2025/12/hapag-lloyd-wins-zemba-s-second-tender-for-pioneering-e-fuel-dep.html*

**Second-tender co-winner.** The captured Aspen Institute source's own headline states: "Hapag-Lloyd and North Sea Container Line have won ZEMBA’s second tender, enabling ZEMBA’s members to abate ocean transport emissions by deploying two pioneering hydrogen-derived e-fuels." *Source: The Aspen Institute, ZEMBA Second Tender Winners, December 17, 2025. https://www.aspeninstitute.org/news/zemba-second-tender-winners/*

**No-fee membership structure.** Join ZEMBA now with no membership fee. It’s an easy yes! *Source: ZEMBA Official Website (shipzemba.org), captured 2026. https://www.shipzemba.org/* *Analytical inference:* zero cost of entry is a deliberate growth strategy; the alliance's negotiating leverage scales with aggregate member freight volume, so low friction to join serves the coalition's commercial position.

# 3. Expected Trajectory and Conversion Triggers

WINDOW CLOSING

**Trajectory timeline.**
- March 9, 2023: the Zero Emission Maritime Buyers Alliance (ZEMBA) is launched by the Aspen Institute, Amazon, Patagonia, and Tchibo.
- 2025-2026: Hapag-Lloyd delivers the inaugural ZEMBA tender's biomethane service on the Singapore-Rotterdam route.
- December 17, 2025: Hapag-Lloyd and North Sea Container Line win ZEMBA's second tender.
- Beginning in 2027: Hapag-Lloyd begins on-water deployment of e-methanol under the second tender.
- March 19, 2026: ZEMBA is named a 2026 Earthshot Prize Nominee.

**Phase 1 completed: inaugural tender.** Global container line Hapag-Lloyd has won ZEMBA’s first tender, will deliver greenhouse gas emissions reduction over 90% as compared to fossil fuel service to ZEMBA members starting in 2025. *Source: The Aspen Institute, Inaugural ZEMBA Tender Completion, 2024. https://www.aspeninstitute.org/news/zemba-inaugural-tender-2024/* The corridor and volume: "more than a dozen ZEMBA members including founding members Amazon, Patagonia, and Tchibo alongside Bauhaus, Brooks Running, DB Journey, Green Worldwide Shipping, Meta, New Balance, Nike, REI Co-op, and Sport-Thieme have collectively committed to purchase the environmental attributes associated with over 1 billion twenty-foot shipping container-miles of zero-emission shipping on a route from Singapore to Rotterdam, Netherlands in 2025-2026." *Source: The Aspen Institute, Inaugural ZEMBA Tender Completion, 2024. https://www.aspeninstitute.org/news/zemba-inaugural-tender-2024/* The realized abatement: "ZEMBA expects members to collectively avoid at least 82,000 metric tonnes of CO2e over two years through Hapag-Lloyd’s independently certified and exclusively waste-based biomethane service." *Source: The Aspen Institute, Inaugural ZEMBA Tender Completion, 2024. https://www.aspeninstitute.org/news/zemba-inaugural-tender-2024/*

**Phase 2 completed: second tender (December 17, 2025).** [conversion_trigger] Through this agreement, ZEMBA members have committed to collectively abate at least 120,000 metric tons of CO₂e over a minimum of three years – with Hapag-Lloyd contributing the lion’s share of these volumes. *Source: Hapag-Lloyd Press Release, December 17, 2025. https://www.hapag-lloyd.com/en/company/press/releases/2025/12/hapag-lloyd-wins-zemba-s-second-tender-for-pioneering-e-fuel-dep.html* The captured Aspen Institute source states the same commitment independently: "This results in at least approximately a combined 120,000 metric tonnes of GHG emissions abated, starting in 2027." *Source: The Aspen Institute, ZEMBA Second Tender Winners, December 17, 2025. https://www.aspeninstitute.org/news/zemba-second-tender-winners/* *Corroboration count:* two independent captured sources (Hapag-Lloyd's own press release and the Aspen Institute's own announcement) state the same 120,000-tonne abatement commitment.

**Conversion trigger: the 2027 on-water deployment.** [conversion_trigger] Beginning in 2027, Hapag-Lloyd will deploy e-methanol on a trans-oceanic lane on large methanol dual-fuel containerships. The e-methanol will be made with very low-carbon hydrogen produced with renewable energy and will deliver a carbon intensity reduction of at least 90% on a lifecycle basis relative to conventional high emission fuel. *Source: Hapag-Lloyd Press Release, December 17, 2025. https://www.hapag-lloyd.com/en/company/press/releases/2025/12/hapag-lloyd-wins-zemba-s-second-tender-for-pioneering-e-fuel-dep.html* *Analytical inference:* this is the trigger that converts ZEMBA from a procurement commitment into a demonstrated, on-water fuel-supply fact; if the e-methanol deployment proves operationally reliable and cost-competitive at that carbon-intensity level once it begins, ZEMBA members gain an auditable Scope 3-relevant credential that non-member shippers will lack.

**Longer-horizon target.** [conversion_trigger] The captured ZEMBA source states its own stated horizon for the sector: "To ensure a reliable, affordable, clean energy future in ocean transportation by 2050 at the latest, we need a rapid increase in innovation and a competitive market for new fuels and technologies." *Source: ZEMBA Official Website (shipzemba.org), captured 2026. https://www.shipzemba.org/* *Analytical inference:* this 2050 horizon frames ZEMBA's two completed tenders as early moves in a multi-decade market-formation effort, not a one-time procurement event.

**Action already open.** [action_now] Contracting remains ongoing, and ZEMBA welcomes additional freight buyers to reach out through ZEMBA’s  website  if interested in joining this deal. *Source: The Aspen Institute, ZEMBA Second Tender Winners, December 17, 2025. https://www.aspeninstitute.org/news/zemba-second-tender-winners/*

**What remains genuinely unstated.** The captured pool does not state a specific date, scope, or fuel type for a third ZEMBA tender, nor a stated membership-count threshold at which non-participation becomes commercially costly; neither figure is asserted here. *Source: ZEMBA Official Website (shipzemba.org), captured 2026. https://www.shipzemba.org/*

# 4. Operational and Cost Implications If It Materializes

MONITORING

**Ocean freight: primary exposure.** Ocean shipping is essential to our economy. 80-90% of cargo is shipped across the ocean. *Source: ZEMBA Official Website (shipzemba.org), captured 2026. https://www.shipzemba.org/* *Operational implication:* for workspaces whose clients are or aspire to become ZEMBA members, the ability to route ocean freight through ZEMBA-contracted carriers is a service capability question, not merely a preference. The captured Hapag-Lloyd source states the winning carrier's own scale: "With a fleet of 305 modern container ships and a total transport capacity of 2.5 million TEU, Hapag-Lloyd is one of the world’s leading liner shipping companies." *Source: Hapag-Lloyd Press Release, December 17, 2025. https://www.hapag-lloyd.com/en/company/press/releases/2025/12/hapag-lloyd-wins-zemba-s-second-tender-for-pioneering-e-fuel-dep.html* and its network reach: "A total of 130 liner services worldwide ensure fast and reliable connections between more than 600 ports on all the continents." *Source: Hapag-Lloyd Press Release, December 17, 2025. https://www.hapag-lloyd.com/en/company/press/releases/2025/12/hapag-lloyd-wins-zemba-s-second-tender-for-pioneering-e-fuel-dep.html* *Analytical inference:* a workspace with an existing Hapag-Lloyd commercial relationship on the lanes ZEMBA's tenders cover is better positioned to reference ZEMBA-contracted volumes in client conversations than one without such a relationship.

**Cost premium: genuinely unstated.** No per-unit or per-TEU cost premium for ZEMBA-contracted e-fuel freight versus conventional bunker freight is stated anywhere in this item's captured pool; none is asserted here. *Source: ZEMBA Official Website (shipzemba.org), captured 2026. https://www.shipzemba.org/*

**Air freight: no direct applicability.** *Operational implication:* every captured source describes ZEMBA as an ocean-shipping-specific initiative (tenders, container lines, trans-oceanic lanes); nothing in the captured pool describes air-freight activity under ZEMBA. Workspaces whose primary mode is air are operationally unaffected; the relevance is commercial and reputational only, per Section 6 below.

# 5. Competitive Implications

COMPETITIVE EDGE

**Carrier stratification is already underway.** Hapag-Lloyd, one of the world’s leading container shipping companies, was selected as the winner of ZEMBA’s inaugural tender. *Source: The Aspen Institute, Inaugural ZEMBA Tender Completion, 2024. https://www.aspeninstitute.org/news/zemba-inaugural-tender-2024/* The captured Aspen Institute second-tender source's own headline: "Hapag-Lloyd and North Sea Container Line have won ZEMBA’s second tender, enabling ZEMBA’s members to abate ocean transport emissions by deploying two pioneering hydrogen-derived e-fuels." *Source: The Aspen Institute, ZEMBA Second Tender Winners, December 17, 2025. https://www.aspeninstitute.org/news/zemba-second-tender-winners/* *Analytical inference:* Hapag-Lloyd is the only carrier to win both ZEMBA tenders; North Sea Container Line is the only co-winner named. A freight forwarder with an established Hapag-Lloyd relationship on the lanes these tenders cover can offer clients a Scope 3-relevant credential that forwarders without that relationship cannot match today.

**Named competitor positioning.** No source in this item's captured pool names a specific competing freight forwarder's positioning relative to ZEMBA or its winning carriers; the pool corroborates the alliance's own procurement mechanism and its cargo-owner and carrier participants but not named-competitor freight-forwarder positioning, and this brief does not invent that data to appear complete. *Source: Hapag-Lloyd Press Release, December 17, 2025. https://www.hapag-lloyd.com/en/company/press/releases/2025/12/hapag-lloyd-wins-zemba-s-second-tender-for-pioneering-e-fuel-dep.html*

# 6. Client Conversation Talking Points

**What the workspace can credibly say:**

- ZEMBA has completed two competitive tender rounds: an inaugural 2024 tender (Hapag-Lloyd, biomethane, Singapore-Rotterdam, at least 82,000 metric tonnes of CO2e avoided over two years) and a second December 17, 2025 tender (Hapag-Lloyd and North Sea Container Line, hydrogen-derived e-fuels, at least 120,000 metric tons of CO2e committed over a minimum of three years, deployment beginning 2027).
- Membership is no-fee and currently exceeds 45 companies, including Amazon, IKEA, and Nike.
- ZEMBA has been named a 2026 Earthshot Prize Nominee.
- Contracting for the second tender remains open; ZEMBA itself invites additional freight buyers to reach out through its own website.

**What to avoid saying:**

- *Legal Confirmation Required:* the captured pool describes ZEMBA members committing to abate CO2e volumes and purchase the environmental attributes of specific shipping activity, but does not state, in any of the five captured sources, the precise mechanism by which an individual member's or a routing freight forwarder's own emissions accounting receives credit for that abatement; this requires confirmation from ZEMBA programme materials or counsel, not this brief.
- Do not quote a cost premium or cost savings figure for ZEMBA-contracted freight; none has been published in the captured source material.
- Do not represent ZEMBA as a regulatory requirement. Every captured source describes it as a voluntary buyers' coalition, not a mandate.

**Questions to pose to clients:**

- Is your company a ZEMBA member or evaluating membership? If not, are your major ocean carriers ZEMBA participants, specifically Hapag-Lloyd or North Sea Container Line?
- Does your sustainability reporting track Scope 3 ocean-freight emissions, and would a ZEMBA-linked routing option be relevant to that reporting?
- Do your major ocean trade lanes overlap with the Singapore-Rotterdam corridor the inaugural tender used, or the trans-oceanic lane the second tender's e-methanol deployment covers from 2027?

# 7. What the Workspace Should Do Now

ACTION REQUIRED

**1. Map client exposure to ZEMBA membership (within 60 days).** *Operational implication:* identify which current or prospective clients are named ZEMBA members (Amazon, Patagonia, Tchibo, IKEA, Nike, and the other companies named in Section 2) or have comparable Scope 3 ocean-freight commitments. For those clients, the workspace's ability to speak to ZEMBA's mechanism and route through ZEMBA-contracted carriers is a capability to assess and communicate.

**2. Engage ZEMBA directly while second-tender contracting remains open.** [action_now] Contracting remains ongoing, and ZEMBA welcomes additional freight buyers to reach out through ZEMBA’s  website  if interested in joining this deal. *Source: The Aspen Institute, ZEMBA Second Tender Winners, December 17, 2025. https://www.aspeninstitute.org/news/zemba-second-tender-winners/* *Operational implication:* this is a stated, currently-open channel, not a future date to wait for.

**3. Establish or review a Hapag-Lloyd commercial relationship on the relevant lanes.** Hapag-Lloyd is the only carrier to win both ZEMBA tenders, with the second tender's e-methanol deployment beginning in 2027 on a trans-oceanic lane. *Source: Hapag-Lloyd Press Release, December 17, 2025. https://www.hapag-lloyd.com/en/company/press/releases/2025/12/hapag-lloyd-wins-zemba-s-second-tender-for-pioneering-e-fuel-dep.html* *Operational implication:* confirm whether existing or prospective commercial terms with Hapag-Lloyd on relevant lanes can be structured to reference ZEMBA-contracted volumes for clients with Scope 3 reporting needs.

**4. Track RFP 3 issuance (monitor on an ongoing basis).** *Analytical inference:* based on the observed 2024-then-2025 tender cadence, a third tender is plausible, though no specific date, scope, or fuel type for it is stated in the captured pool; the ZEMBA website's own "The Latest" section is the tracking point named by the source itself.

**5. Monitor membership growth past the current 45+ threshold.** *Analytical inference:* the point at which non-participation becomes commercially costly for a client or a carrier is not established in any captured source and is not asserted here; growth beyond the current membership count is the signal to watch.

# 8. Sources

| 4 | Zero Emission Maritime Buyers Alliance (ZEMBA) Announces Successful Completion of Inaugural Collective Tender | The Aspen Institute | Not stated in captured text (URL references the 2024 inaugural tender; body text states "starting in 2025" for service delivery) | Press release | https://www.aspeninstitute.org/news/zemba-inaugural-tender-2024/ |

metadata.what_is_it: A market intelligence signal, anchored in five captured sources (the Aspen Institute's launch and two tender announcements, ZEMBA's own website, and Hapag-Lloyd's own press release), tracking the Zero Emission Maritime Buyers Alliance (ZEMBA): a no-fee cargo-owner buyers' coalition, co-founded by the Aspen Institute, Amazon, Patagonia, and Tchibo, that has completed two competitive fuel-procurement tenders with Hapag-Lloyd and North Sea Container Line and is now a 2026 Earthshot Prize Nominee.
metadata.why_matters: Freight forwarders serving cargo owners with Scope 3 ocean-freight ambitions face a coalition that has moved from launch announcement to two completed, carrier-committed tenders: an inaugural 2024 award (Hapag-Lloyd, biomethane, Singapore-Rotterdam, at least 82,000 metric tonnes of CO2e avoided) and a December 17, 2025 second award (Hapag-Lloyd and North Sea Container Line, hydrogen-derived e-fuels, at least 120,000 metric tons of CO2e committed, deployment beginning 2027). Membership already exceeds 45 companies including Amazon, IKEA, and Nike, and second-tender contracting remains open. A workspace with an established Hapag-Lloyd relationship on the relevant lanes is positioned to speak to a live, named commercial mechanism in client conversations; one without such a relationship faces a growing gap in that specific conversation.
key_data: 99% of vessels on the water today operate on high-emission fuels (ZEMBA)
45+ member companies as of the Hapag-Lloyd second-tender release including Amazon; IKEA; Nike
Inaugural tender: at least 82000 metric tonnes of CO2e avoided over two years (Hapag-Lloyd biomethane; Singapore-Rotterdam; 2025-2026)
Second tender: at least 120000 metric tons of CO2e committed over a minimum of three years (Hapag-Lloyd e-methanol plus North Sea Container Line; deployment beginning 2027)

entries.body:
# 1. What's Moving and What Triggered It

MONITORING

**The trigger -- Middle East conflict and Strait of Hormuz disruption, March-June 2026**

The captured source's own data-table heading reads, verbatim: "Air Cargo Market in Detail - March 2026" *Source: IATA, "Middle East Disruption Impacts Cargo Markets, Demand Falls 4.8% in March," 29 April 2026. https://www.iata.org/en/pressroom/2026-releases/2026-04-29-03/*

The captured source states, verbatim: "Total demand, measured in cargo tonne-kilometers (CTK), fell by 4.8% compared to March 2025 levels (-5.5% for international operations)." *Source: IATA, "Middle East Disruption Impacts Cargo Markets, Demand Falls 4.8% in March," 29 April 2026. https://www.iata.org/en/pressroom/2026-releases/2026-04-29-03/*

The captured source states, verbatim: "Middle Eastern carriers saw a 54.3% year-on-year decrease in demand for air cargo in March, the weakest performance of all regions. Capacity decreased by 52.4% year-on-year." *Source: IATA, "Middle East Disruption Impacts Cargo Markets, Demand Falls 4.8% in March," 29 April 2026. https://www.iata.org/en/pressroom/2026-releases/2026-04-29-03/*

The captured source states, verbatim: "Jet fuel prices rose sharply in March, up 106.6% year-on-year, alongside a 43.1% increase in crude oil prices and a 320% surge in refining margins." *Source: IATA, "Middle East Disruption Impacts Cargo Markets, Demand Falls 4.8% in March," 29 April 2026. https://www.iata.org/en/pressroom/2026-releases/2026-04-29-03/*

*Analytical inference:* the simultaneous March collapse in Middle Eastern carrier demand and capacity, alongside a jet-fuel price surge, is the earliest data point in this pool confirming that the Middle East conflict had already reshaped global air cargo economics before the April and May data below.

**Partial demand recovery in April -- but Gulf disruption persists**

The captured source states, verbatim: "Total demand, measured in cargo tonne-kilometers (CTK), increased by 4.0% compared to April 2025 levels (+4.0% for international operations). Capacity, measured in available cargo tonne-kilometers (ACTK), decreased by -0.4% compared to April 2025 (-0.9% for international operations)." *Source: IATA, "Air Cargo Demand Up 4.0% in April Amid Middle East Disruption," 28 May 2026. https://www.iata.org/en/pressroom/2026-releases/05-28-air-cargo-demand-up-april-middle-east-disruption/*

The captured source states, verbatim: "Middle Eastern carriers saw a -18.2% year-on-year decrease in demand for air cargo in April, the weakest performance of all regions. Capacity decreased by -22.9% year-on-year." *Source: IATA, "Air Cargo Demand Up 4.0% in April Amid Middle East Disruption," 28 May 2026. https://www.iata.org/en/pressroom/2026-releases/05-28-air-cargo-demand-up-april-middle-east-disruption/*

The captured source states, verbatim: "Jet fuel prices rose sharply in April, up 121.1% year-on-year, alongside a 77.7% increase in crude oil prices." *Source: IATA, "Air Cargo Demand Up 4.0% in April Amid Middle East Disruption," 28 May 2026. https://www.iata.org/en/pressroom/2026-releases/05-28-air-cargo-demand-up-april-middle-east-disruption/*

*Operational implication:* headline demand recovery (CTK +4.0%) coexisted with continued capacity contraction (ACTK -0.4%) and a still-collapsed Middle East region (-18.2% demand, -22.9% capacity); a workspace reading only the headline CTK figure would miss that the underlying Gulf disruption had not resolved.

**Escalation on the ground -- Fujairah and the Strait of Hormuz**

The captured source states, verbatim: "Flights bound for Dubai and Sharjah are being held or diverted, following a drone attack on a key oil industrial zone in Fujairah that has disrupted UAE air space." *Source: Flexport, "Middle East Escalation Disrupts Global Ocean and Air Freight Networks," updated 2 June 2026. https://www.flexport.com/blog/middle-east-escalation-disrupts-global-ocean-and-air-freight-networks/*

The captured source states, verbatim: "Oil prices jumped more than 7% following Tasnim" *Source: Flexport, "Middle East Escalation Disrupts Global Ocean and Air Freight Networks," updated 2 June 2026. https://www.flexport.com/blog/middle-east-escalation-disrupts-global-ocean-and-air-freight-networks/*

*Analytical inference:* the Fujairah drone attack and the oil-price spike that followed the Strait-of-Hormuz closure threat are the physical and financial transmission mechanisms behind the fuel-cost and capacity figures reported by IATA and Xeneta above -- this is not a market moving independently of the conflict, it is the conflict's direct pricing signature.

**Spot rate surge: May 2026**

The captured source states, verbatim: "Global air cargo spot rates rose 41% year-on-year in May to an average of $3.40 per kg, driven by resilient demand, constrained capacity and ongoing geopolitical disruptions, according to Xeneta." *Source: Xeneta / Stat Times, "Global air cargo spot rates surge 41% in May amid tensions," 6 June 2026. https://www.stattimes.com/air-cargo/global-air-cargo-spot-rates-surge-41-in-may-amid-tensions-1359396*

The captured source states, verbatim: "The dynamic load factor also climbed two percentage points to 61%, reflecting stronger capacity utilisation across the industry." *Source: Xeneta / Stat Times, "Global air cargo spot rates surge 41% in May amid tensions," 6 June 2026. https://www.stattimes.com/air-cargo/global-air-cargo-spot-rates-surge-41-in-may-amid-tensions-1359396*

The captured source states, verbatim: "average full market air cargo rates were flat in week 21 at $3.23 per kilo, but compared to the same period last year, restricted capacity, high jet fuel costs, and greater use of freighter aircraft drove a rate increase of 35%." *Source: WorldACD / Global Trade Magazine, "Global Air Cargo Markets Show Stabilization in Mid-May 2026," 2 June 2026. https://www.globaltrademag.com/global-air-cargo-markets-show-stabilization-in-mid-may-2026/*

The captured source states, verbatim: "These figures are based on more than 500,000 weekly transactions covered by WorldACD’s data, resulting in average worldwide spot rates being 50% higher year on year." *Source: WorldACD / Global Trade Magazine, "Global Air Cargo Markets Show Stabilization in Mid-May 2026," 2 June 2026. https://www.globaltrademag.com/global-air-cargo-markets-show-stabilization-in-mid-may-2026/*

The captured source states, verbatim: "Spot rates from MESA rose 59% year on year to $4.26 per kilo, while spot rates from most other regions increased by more than 40% year on year" *Source: WorldACD / Global Trade Magazine, "Global Air Cargo Markets Show Stabilization in Mid-May 2026," 2 June 2026. https://www.globaltrademag.com/global-air-cargo-markets-show-stabilization-in-mid-may-2026/*

**Gulf capacity still barely half its pre-war level**

The captured source states, verbatim: "compared to pre-war levels in week 7, capacity is down by nearly one third (32%), largely due to reductions for the Gulf, where capacity is barely half its pre-war levels (48%)." *Source: WorldACD / Global Trade Magazine, "Global Air Cargo Markets Show Stabilization in Mid-May 2026," 2 June 2026. https://www.globaltrademag.com/global-air-cargo-markets-show-stabilization-in-mid-may-2026/*

The captured source states, verbatim: "Airlines cut 13,000 flights in May, and industry observers expect further schedule changes as aviation fuel prices are unlikely to decline significantly in the near term." *Source: WorldACD / Stat Times, "Global air cargo tonnage, pricing and capacity decline in early May," 18 May 2026. https://www.stattimes.com/amp/air-cargo/global-air-cargo-tonnage-pricing-and-capacity-decline-in-early-may-1359159*

*Operational implication:* for workspaces whose air freight routing touches Dubai, Sharjah, Abu Dhabi, Doha, or other Gulf hub airports, this is the single most decision-relevant figure in this brief: capacity at roughly half the pre-war level, more than two months into the disruption, with no confirmed restoration date anywhere in this pool.

---

# 2. Who's Driving It and What They Want

**Geopolitical actors**

The captured source states, verbatim: "U.S. forces struck Iranian radar and drone control sites on Goruk and Qeshm Island after a U.S. drone was shot down over international waters. Iran's IRGC responded by firing ballistic missiles at U.S. forces in Kuwait" *Source: Flexport, "Middle East Escalation Disrupts Global Ocean and Air Freight Networks," updated 2 June 2026. https://www.flexport.com/blog/middle-east-escalation-disrupts-global-ocean-and-air-freight-networks/*

The captured source states, verbatim: "Trump convened his national security team Friday, May 29 to make a "final determination" on a ceasefire framework, but the meeting ended without a decision." *Source: Flexport, "Middle East Escalation Disrupts Global Ocean and Air Freight Networks," updated 2 June 2026. https://www.flexport.com/blog/middle-east-escalation-disrupts-global-ocean-and-air-freight-networks/*

The captured source states, verbatim: "The U.S. has insisted any deal must include the reopening of the Strait, Iran renouncing nuclear weapons development, and the removal of its enriched uranium stockpile. Iran has repeatedly rejected those terms." *Source: Flexport, "Middle East Escalation Disrupts Global Ocean and Air Freight Networks," updated 2 June 2026. https://www.flexport.com/blog/middle-east-escalation-disrupts-global-ocean-and-air-freight-networks/*

*Analytical inference:* the U.S. and Iran are the two parties whose direct military exchanges and unresolved ceasefire terms are setting the timeline for Gulf air and ocean capacity restoration; no third party in this pool has the standing to accelerate that timeline independently.

**Airlines and capacity holders**

The captured source states, verbatim: "Freighter operations by Gulf-based carriers have largely recovered, although passenger services are not expected to fully return until conflict conditions stabilise and traveller confidence improves." *Source: WorldACD / Stat Times, "Global air cargo tonnage, pricing and capacity decline in early May," 18 May 2026. https://www.stattimes.com/amp/air-cargo/global-air-cargo-tonnage-pricing-and-capacity-decline-in-early-may-1359159*

The captured source states, verbatim: "Rising fuel costs have also led airlines to reduce or cancel unprofitable routes, particularly regional services operated by narrowbody aircraft, although the impact on cargo capacity has remained limited." *Source: WorldACD / Stat Times, "Global air cargo tonnage, pricing and capacity decline in early May," 18 May 2026. https://www.stattimes.com/amp/air-cargo/global-air-cargo-tonnage-pricing-and-capacity-decline-in-early-may-1359159*

*Analytical inference:* the freighter-versus-passenger recovery gap named above means Gulf-based carriers' CARGO capacity is closer to normal than their overall commercial capacity -- a workspace evaluating a Gulf-based carrier partner should ask specifically about freighter, not passenger-belly, capacity.

The captured source states, verbatim, as IATA's Director General: "With dedicated freighters carrying much of the growth, air cargo is once again keeping supply chains moving amid trade disruptions. The coming months will test how well the sector can absorb continued geopolitical uncertainty and elevated operating costs" *Source: IATA, "Air Cargo Demand Up 4.0% in April Amid Middle East Disruption," 28 May 2026. https://www.iata.org/en/pressroom/2026-releases/05-28-air-cargo-demand-up-april-middle-east-disruption/*

**Shippers and forwarders**

The captured source states, verbatim: "Shippers clearly have a sense of ‘here we go again’ in terms of rate volatility, but they are adjusting and buying time by temporarily accepting the surcharges that come with extending existing capacity contracts." *Source: Xeneta / Stat Times, "Global air cargo spot rates surge 41% in May amid tensions," 6 June 2026. https://www.stattimes.com/air-cargo/global-air-cargo-spot-rates-surge-41-in-may-amid-tensions-1359396*

*Analytical inference:* shippers accepting short-term surcharges rather than signing new long-term capacity contracts is itself a market signal -- it indicates the demand side does not yet trust the current rate environment to be the new normal, which is consistent with Xeneta's own forecast of near-term softening (Section 3).

---

# 3. Expected Trajectory and Conversion Triggers

WINDOW CLOSING

**Near-term softening signal -- but not recovery**

The captured source states, verbatim: "Despite the sharp increase in rates, Xeneta believes pricing pressures on shippers may begin to ease in June as capacity returns and demand growth moderates." *Source: Xeneta / Stat Times, "Global air cargo spot rates surge 41% in May amid tensions," 6 June 2026. https://www.stattimes.com/air-cargo/global-air-cargo-spot-rates-surge-41-in-may-amid-tensions-1359396*

The captured source states, verbatim: "Long-term contract rates, which increased 22% year-on-year, eased after reaching a peak at the end of April, suggesting the market may have already passed its pricing high point." *Source: Xeneta / Stat Times, "Global air cargo spot rates surge 41% in May amid tensions," 6 June 2026. https://www.stattimes.com/air-cargo/global-air-cargo-spot-rates-surge-41-in-may-amid-tensions-1359396*

The captured source states, verbatim: "Further moderation is expected during the northern hemisphere summer period, when additional passenger aircraft capacity typically returns to the market." *Source: Xeneta / Stat Times, "Global air cargo spot rates surge 41% in May amid tensions," 6 June 2026. https://www.stattimes.com/air-cargo/global-air-cargo-spot-rates-surge-41-in-may-amid-tensions-1359396*

The captured source states, verbatim, from Xeneta's own Chief Airfreight Officer: "I would not be surprised to see year-on-year spot rate comparisons decline in June, especially as there are not a lot of industry verticals that are booming at the moment." *Source: Xeneta / Stat Times, "Global air cargo spot rates surge 41% in May amid tensions," 6 June 2026. https://www.stattimes.com/air-cargo/global-air-cargo-spot-rates-surge-41-in-may-amid-tensions-1359396*

**Gulf capacity gap is structural until the conflict resolves**

The captured source states, verbatim: "Even if Iran and the U.S. negotiate an end to hostilities, analysts warn it could take months for normal traffic to resume in the Strait." *Source: Flexport, "Middle East Escalation Disrupts Global Ocean and Air Freight Networks," updated 2 June 2026. https://www.flexport.com/blog/middle-east-escalation-disrupts-global-ocean-and-air-freight-networks/*

The captured source states, verbatim: "Some spot rates were up by as much as 113% compared with late February." *Source: Xeneta / Stat Times, "Global air cargo spot rates surge 41% in May amid tensions," 6 June 2026. https://www.stattimes.com/air-cargo/global-air-cargo-spot-rates-surge-41-in-may-amid-tensions-1359396*

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the U.S.-stated ceasefire terms described in Section 2, which the U.S. has insisted any deal "must include," are a negotiating position reported by the captured source, not a ratified agreement; whether or when those terms bind either party is not something this brief resolves.

**Conversion triggers to watch**

- Ceasefire covering Strait of Hormuz reopening: the U.S. has insisted any deal must include the reopening of the Strait, Iran renouncing nuclear weapons development, and the removal of its enriched uranium stockpile; Iran has repeatedly rejected those terms as of this pool's most recent capture. *Source: Flexport, "Middle East Escalation Disrupts Global Ocean and Air Freight Networks," updated 2 June 2026. https://www.flexport.com/blog/middle-east-escalation-disrupts-global-ocean-and-air-freight-networks/*
